It turns out Real American Freestyle Wrestling owes as much to Hulk Hogan as it does to a father-son wrestling match. There is a chain between them, connecting the controversial WWE legend to Chad Bronstein via their fellow co-founders: another WWE icon in Eric Bischoff, and one of the US’s top coaches in Izzy Martinez.

If you’re an American reader, you’ll easily differentiate between “professional wrestling”, which the late Hogan dominated (allegedly through persistent politicking, mind), and “amateur wrestling”. The latter has always stood out as a misnomer to this writer; while pro wrestler Hogan, up until his death last July, was a “Real American” per his entrance music, amateur wrestling is the real sport – an Olympic one, and a staple in high schools around the country. Actually, one can get more granular: the variety practised in schools and colleges is folkstyle, while the Olympic version is freestyle.

Yet a sport as big as amateur wrestling was missing something. While pro wrestling has had the WWE, American football the NFL, basketball the NBA, and baseball the MLB, amateur wrestling was lacking a big, three-letter brand to make it a true, commercial, spectator sport. And then came RAF.

Exactly one year on from its debut event, Bronstein reflects on the promotion’s origins while speaking to The Independent. “My son is 10, but when he was seven, we were wrestling,” says the 39-year-old CEO, who began in ad-tech before working with Hogan on Real American Beer. “My wife was going through something difficult, and we just fell back in love with the sport, because I’ve wrestled my whole life.

“I was trying to figure out something unique for the sport. I told Hulk the idea, he was like: ‘Brother, I love it.’” It’s a good Hogan impression, in fairness. “He always talked about Bischoff being a part of it. Then my son’s wrestling coach told me: ‘Go see Izzy Martinez.’ I’m like: ‘He can really be my lynchpin in the wrestling.’”

From day one, RAF has been filling arenas in the US with monthly events, showing the appetite for the sport domestically. Yet this summer brought the first international event, in Georgia, with a Russian card coming in September – the first of those countries navigating a fraught relationship with the EU, and the latter still invading Ukraine, it must be noted.

open image in gallery RAF co-founder and CEO Chad Bronstein ( Real American Freestyle )

Still, “Athletes want to compete against the best, they don’t care what country it is,” Bronstein says. “Wrestling is a very international sport. Georgia felt like the World Cup for us. You had all these neighbouring countries coming: Russians, Armenians, people from Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan. Canada is huge in wrestling, we’ve been approached to go to France and other places. We’re going to Turkey, we’re talking about Uzbekistan and Abu Dhabi.

“Our plan is to do one international event every month going into 2027. The UK will definitely be on the list. Wrestling there isn’t as popular as in the US, but in the UK you could start wrestling at four years old – same as here. Whatever sport you play, if I’m a parent, I'd send my kid to wrestling because it gives them confidence and self-defence.”

An intriguing component in RAF’s success has been tapping into the fanbase of mixed martial arts (MMA) juggernaut the UFC, which has lent a number of its fighters to RAF this year.

Arman Tsarukyan, who has struggled to secure a deserved UFC title shot, has been one of RAF’s most dependable wrestlers while he awaits his next MMA fight. Since his last UFC outing in November, he has wrestled eight times with RAF – and will do so again after facing Mauricio Ruffy in the Octagon in September. His colleague, Merab Dvalishvili, very recently a UFC champion, has also emerged as a standout in RAF, and he insists that we should not be so surprised that the UFC – not always the kindest of operators – is letting its fighters wrestle on the side.

“Not at all,” the Georgian says. “The UFC has been very good to me, and respects that I want to keep active in between fights. Plus, it keeps me in shape and ready.”

open image in gallery Tyron Woodley (right) during his reign as UFC welterweight champion ( Getty )

It’s a sentiment echoed by former UFC champion Tyron Woodley, who will headline the Russian event against Khamzat Chimaev, who only lost his UFC title three months ago.

“Hell no, the UFC need to do this. They just had to cash out $375m in a class-action lawsuit. RAF is not competing [with the UFC], and wrestlers make up almost 75 per cent of their champions, so why wouldn’t you support wrestling?

“Nobody’s really going to get injured; they can get injured in practice just as likely. And guys stay in shape, so when you ask them for a last-minute UFC fight, they don’t have to say ‘no’. The thing about wrestling is, it’s such a complementary sport, you don’t have to pick and choose.

“That’s why you see guys that just recently lost a UFC championship, or current guys on the Olympic ladder, going against each other. It doesn’t knock their brand if they lose a wrestling match and then fight for a UFC championship. It’s so separate. So, I think it’s smart on the UFC’s part.”

Bronstein, who represents ex-UFC champion Julianna Pena, explains he’s “built a relationship over several years with [UFC CBO] Hunter Campbell. We’re not an MMA organisation, so we’re not competitive [against the UFC]. If you can wrestle five times a year, you’re building your brand and getting better at a sport that’s very helpful to fighting.

“Merab Dvalishvili just beat Henry Cejudo, an Olympic gold-medalist wrestler. Bo Nickal is great at wrestling and fighting, and he gets to do both. Injury-wise, wrestling is six minutes. Could you get injured? Yes. Is it a high probability? No, not if your body is in the right form.”

open image in gallery Former UFC champion Khamzat Chimaev in action in RAF ( Real American Freestyle )

Woodley was considered one of the UFC’s greatest champions before a run of losses that extended past MMA and into boxing, including a KO by Jake Paul. Ahead of his RAF debut, he’s surely relishing the chance to compete without getting hit in the head.

Yet he argues that wrestling, his first love, “is a harder sport than boxing, MMA. It’s probably the most difficult sport you can do.

“You can imagine a period being two or three minutes, but there’s so much going on. With chain wrestling, one move is set up, another move defends that, you go to another. It’s static strength the entire time, focusing and resisting at the same time, then the top and bottom positions.

“And the conditioning is very tough. I was walking around fat, happy, looking like Yogi Bear. I was 220lb. I already lost 30lb [since training for RAF]. I could never lose 30lb just boxing. I haven’t weighed this since the beginning of my MMA career.

“Also, it’s one of the few sports that every body type is allowed to do: big, little, short, tall; long arm, short arm; strong, flexible. So, it’s hard to prepare. There are styles that are more scrambly and funky like Ben Askren, or more explosive and aggressive style like Khamzat.”

Askren’s story is surely the most inspirational in RAF. An Olympic wrestler turned MMA champion, Askren wrestled ex-UFC title holder Belal Muhammad in July, one year after undergoing an emergency double-lung transplant.

open image in gallery Merab Dvalishvili and Henry Cejudo have wrestled each other twice in RAF, having previously fought each other in the UFC ( Real American Freestyle )

A valiant Askren lost, but as his good friend Woodley notes: “You got people losing by 18 points and coming back. The back and forth gives the spirit of MMA. You can never count somebody out.”

So it was for Dvalishvili when he wrestled Cejudo in July, two years after their UFC showdown. But when the former UFC champions rematched in RAF on Saturday, one of America’s greatest-ever fighters exacted revenge; Cejudo pinned the Georgian in 36 seconds.

It’s not just the scheduled action that has enthralled, though; Tsarukyan’s brawl with Georgio Poullas and Chimaev’s with Dillon Danis also went viral, just two cases of RAF attracting millions of views on social media – to complement its streaming deal with Fox Nation. For better or worse, it feels like anything can happen at an RAF event.

What’s more, UFC legend Michael Bisping suggested he was offered $500,000 to compete in RAF, with that alleged number easily eclipsing the purses that most UFC bouts bring.

“There’s never been a league that succeeded in wrestling, so if we fail, who’s going to come in after us?” Bronstein asks. “It’s important that we exist. We’re just getting started.”

President Donald Trump was warned against attacking Iran in February by U.S. intelligence chiefs, who suggested it could backfire and usher in an even more hard-line regime, according to a report.

The Wall Street Journal reports that the then-director of national intelligence and military veteran Tulsi Gabbard was summoned to the Oval Office to discuss the issue before strikes were launched on February 28.

Trump was reportedly buoyed at the time by the success of the previous summer’s Operation Midnight Hammer attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities and the removal of Nicolas Maduro from power in Venezuela and wanted her assessment on the proposed new assault.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had reportedly pushed for military action, claimed the Islamic Republic was in a weaker condition than ever before so there was an opportunity to extinguish its nuclear ambitions once and for all.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump was reportedly advised by Tulsi Gabbard, his former director of national intelligence, that any attack on Iran could backfire ( AFP/Getty )

But according to The Journal’s sources, Gabbard told Trump killing Ayatollah Ali Khamenei would only usher in a more authoritarian government more likely to seek weapons of mass destruction.

The president was also reportedly told Iran would likely respond to airstrikes by shutting off the Strait of Hormuz to spike oil prices and by retaliating against America’s regional allies, which is exactly what happened.

Military top brass is said to have cautioned Trump the proposed operation would mean casualties, dwindling munitions supplies and overstretched resources.

As has been previously reported, Vice President JD Vance also advised him against embarking on the conflict but vowed to support him if he did choose to do so.

open image in gallery The president was reportedly told that Iran would close the Strait of Hormuz shipping route in the event of U.S. strikes ( WANA )

Ultimately, according to the Journal, Trump was persuaded by the arguments put forward by his Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine and Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, who laid out detailed plans for disabling the country with Israel’s help.

Operation Epic Fury was duly launched on February 28 and Khamenei was killed on the first day of the strikes, inspiring an initial wave of euphoria from Trump that quickly gave way once it became clear that the knock-on consequences outlined by Gabbard – who left the administration in May – had come to pass.

The president has since veered wildly from issuing apocalyptic threats against Iran to insisting its new leadership is desperate to sign a peace deal while privately expressing bafflement about its refusal to bow to his persistent military pressure.

open image in gallery Iran has yet to back down in the conflict, which is approaching its seventh month ( AFP/Getty )

Under pressure from Gulf allies like Saudi Arabia and Qatar to cease the fighting and from Republicans at home mindful of the unpopular war’s impact on their midterm election prospects, Trump now finds himself struggling to end a conflict he initially claimed would take six weeks to conduct but which is now entering its sixth month.

The 60-day period for negotiating a peace agreement stipulated by the memorandum of understanding the two sides signed on June 17 has now lapsed, leading the president to turn to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to try to crush Tehran financially with his new Operation Economic Outcast sanctions.

But with 3,000 Iranians and 18 U.S. servicemembers dead and another 756 troops injured, oil prices high and American assets damaged and drained, the problem of ending the hostilities without losing face is becoming increasingly acute.

White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told the Journal in a statement that Trump has succeeded in decimating Iran’s military and its nuclear facilities and will now do the same to its economy.

“He will never allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon,” she said. “It would be wise for Iran to reach a deal. Otherwise, they know what could happen.”

The Independent has reached out to the White House for further comment.

With no tall trees reaching to the sky, Alaska's North Slope tundra can look desolate — especially to outsiders from the Lower 48 who are used to in-your-face greenery.

But up close, “the tundra's kind of like the jungle,” said Adam Bloom, a Florida Atlantic University plant biology student. Except this lush Arctic jungle tops out at about 10 inches (25 centimeters).

Together with Jake Francis, a professor at the university, Bloom walked through the spongy soil that was frozen solid a few weeks earlier. They towered over the knee-high dwarf birch trees. Showy rhododendrons didn't reach the backs of their shoes as they walk in the North Slope, a vast and sparsely populated treeless area stretching from the Brooks mountain range to the Arctic Ocean.

For centuries, Arctic cold has kept plant life small, a sort of dollhouse of Earth's miniatures. The extreme environment has long given researchers a unique perspective on what makes plants grow, insight that would be hard to obtain elsewhere. Now it offers them one of the world’s most useful windows on how climate change affects plant life, with the Arctic warming four times faster than the rest of Earth, especially in the winter. For example, researchers at the Toolik Field Station, 200 miles (320 kilometers) north of the Arctic Circle, are studying whether plants facing these harsh conditions evolve to compete or cooperate with one another.

Studies show that the colder and further north in the Arctic, the smaller the plant life. There are several reasons, but the main one is that life is rough in the winter. Anything that protrudes above the shallow, insulating snow cover is more prone to being damaged by the cold and wind or eaten by wildlife, said plant ecologist Anne Bjorkman of the University of Gothenburg in Sweden.

Plus the frozen permafrost doesn't allow roots to grow too deep, she said.

Earth's miniatures are growing

But the cold is weakening and the miniatures are stretching. This part of Alaska is about 4.8 degrees (2.7 degrees Celsius) warmer than it was 40 years ago mostly because of the burning of coal, oil and gas.

“Plants that are already there are growing taller,” Bjorkman said, adding that they're likely to grow even taller in the future.

And they are getting greener. Some of the long-term studies here are “trying to understand what controls how much plants grow, what controls how green it is,” and how all that is changing, said Columbia University ecologist Duncan Menge.

Meanwhile, taller plants that previously couldn't survive the cold are moving in, Bjorkman said.

This process, called shrubification, can accelerate warming because of how the plants trap heat, said University of Colorado plant ecologist Sarah Elmendorf. Canopies of the taller, darker shrubs stick out of the snow and absorb more energy from the sun than the blanket of white snow, which reflects heat back.

“It's certainly a major fingerprint of change that we can see,” she said.

Darker tundra absorbing more radiation is “one of the main reasons for what we call arctic amplification, which causes climate change to accelerate” especially in the Arctic, Menge said.

The shrubs also trap more snow. That snow warms the ground below and allows microbes during the winter to release more of the heat-trapping gas methane, Elmendorf said. The added greenery from the taller plants and shrubs could compensate somewhat by absorbing more carbon dioxide, she said.

Expanding stands of willows seem to be providing more shade to streams and changing the ecology of fish, insects and birds, according to Chris Neill and Linda Deegan of the Woodwell Climate Research Center. They are conducting a multiyear study to see if an ecosystem adapts and even genetically evolves to handle the stress of climate change. If that is happening, it offers hope for the survival of some of the most fragile Arctic ecosystems, Deegan said.

Using a magnifying lens to appreciate tiny plants

During a foray around Toolik Lake, Francis carried a knuckle-sized magnifying lens around his neck like a locket, using it to reveal the wonder of the tiny flora at his feet.

“Tiny changes in a tiny jungle make a big difference,” said Francis, an Arctic newcomer.

Big trees in Francis' home base of Florida are showy and amaze people because they're so easy to see, he said. But here on the spongy tussocks — clumps of plants that jut upward, making walking an ankle-turning adventure — Francis said, “we have three or four different species of flowering plants growing. We have mosses. We have liverworts and it's the same thing. Layers growing on top of plants on top of plants on top of plants. But it's not yelling at us.”

“You have to get down there and stop and look,” Francis said. “You could walk right past it and not even see it. And so this is what to me is cool.”

What helps survival, competition or cooperation?

These plants are competing for sun, nutrients, water and especially pollination in this harsh environment of limited but intense sunlight. Francis and his students are examining if it's more cooperative than the long assumed life-or-death competition. Francis' team focuses on a specific parasitic plant — the Arctic lousewort — that they think is getting a bad rap. The Arctic lousewort taps into the roots of nearby plants to suck out nutrients.

Sure, it's a vampire, siphoning resources from its neighbors. But doctoral student Jonathan Carcache theorizes that the lousewort is helping its neighbors as much as stealing from them. That's because its dramatic shaft of purple flowers catches the attention of the not-so-plentiful bumblebees here “like a billboard that advertises pollination,” he said. And once that sought-after bee arrives, everyone gets pollinated.

To test their theory, Carcache and Bloom play bee. It's a painstaking, difficult task that they split between them. Bloom uses tweezers to remove a plant's male parts, and back at the lab he uses a mechanical device to shake out the pollen. It takes several hours each night to produce less than a teaspoon full of microscopic pollen grains.

Then Carcache finishes the job, belly-first on the ground and trying not to crush any of the plants they have come to study. Wearing a net over his head and nitrile gloves to protect him from swarming mosquitoes, he takes a paintbrush to dip grains of pollen on just the right female parts of neighboring heather blossoms.

By doing the bees' job, Carcache and Bloom hope to figure out whether the plants around the parasite are pollinated more than those further away. If so, there's a fair trade taking place, rather than one plant simply taking advantage of others.

Amid the stresses of the Arctic, scientists are rethinking the idea that all life is a cutthroat competition with winners and losers. It might be more about mutualism, with plant species cooperating so that everybody survives, like the lousewort and its neighbors, Francis said.

“It would be wonderful if humans were the same way,” Francis said.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: Help us test binoculars with the RSPB and birding experts
News.content:
At Telegraph Recommended, we test hundreds of products each year, and we rely on our community members to help verify our experts’ findings.

We currently have an upcoming opportunity for Telegraph readers to help test the latest binoculars for birdwatching with the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB).

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

Sports.title: Three World Cup winners part of investment group buying own top flight club for just £34m
Sports.content:
THREE World Cup winners are part of an investment group that has bought a 90 per cent stake in Portuguese top-flight club Estrela da Amadora.

Thomas Muller, Mats Hummels and Lucas Hernandez are among the football stars involved in the takeover, alongside former Bayern Munich goalkeeper Yann Sommer.



The German-led consortium has completed a deal worth around £34million to acquire the majority stake in the Lisbon-based club’s professional football operation.

The deal was officially confirmed by Estrela on Tuesday, with the consortium led by ADvantage and LEAD, backed by the KI Group.



Muller and Hummels were part of Germany‘s 2014 World Cup-winning squad, while Hernandez was a member of France‘s 2018 World Cup-winning team.

Sommer, who currently plays for Club Brugge, is also part of the new ownership group.



The four former Bayern players are not expected to be involved in the day-to-day running of the club.

Instead, 35-year-old Johannes Mosmang has been appointed president of SAD – the consortiums combined – replacing Paulo Lopo.

Mosmang spent around a decade working in Bayern’s player-management department and is understood to know the quartet from his time at the German giants.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He said: “Estrela Amadora is a traditional Portuguese football club with deep roots in Amadora, a unique identity, and a passionate community.



“The club also boasts a special feature: its own stadium.

“We are highly motivated to begin this new chapter and to implement a project in a disciplined and sustainable manner, one that the fans, the community, and everyone associated with Estrela can be proud of.”

The takeover represents a remarkable rise in Estrela’s fortunes.



The club was declared insolvent in 2011, with its senior side eventually re-established in the lower reaches of Portuguese football.

After a merger with Sintra in 2020, Estrela returned to the third tier before climbing back into the top flight in 2023.

They have remained in Portugal‘s Primeira Liga ever since.



The scale of the investment is even more striking given that Paulo Lopo reportedly acquired the club for just £61,000 in 2020.

Six years later, 90 per cent of the professional football operation has changed hands for £34m.

The new owners will now hope their star-studded backing can help Estrela establish themselves among Portugal’s elite and continue their rapid rise.

Sports.title: Why has Savinho changed his name?
Sports.content:
SPURS have completed the £85million signing of Brazil winger Savio, and fans were quick to spot something odd about the announcement.

The player Manchester City signed as Savinho two years ago has arrived in north London with a different name.



Why has Savinho changed his name to Savio?

Neither Tottenham nor Savio has given a reason for the switch, and no explanation appeared in the club’s announcement.

What is clear is that he has gone back to the name he used before joining City.



His full name is Savio Moreira de Oliveira, and Savinho is simply the Portuguese diminutive of that, roughly translating to “little Savio”.

He wore Savio on his shirt at Troyes and during his breakout loan spell at Girona, where he made his name in La Liga.

The switch to Savinho came when he joined City in July 2024, and he did explain that one at the time.

Brazil put Savinho on his shirt for his first senior call-up in March of that year.

Speaking to the Man City website, he said he hoped “the Savinho name brings me some good luck”.

Brazilian players commonly go by nicknames on their shirts, but whether the return to Savio reflects superstition, personal preference or simply a fresh start remains a mystery at this time.



Savio was named by his dad after former Brazil and Real Madrid winger Savio Bortolini.

Why has Savio joined Tottenham?

City boss Enzo Maresca said Savio made it clear he wanted to leave the club.

Spurs will pay an initial £75million with a further £10million in add-ons, of which around £5million is effectively guaranteed, according to Sky Sports.

Savio has signed a five-year deal and will wear the number 17 shirt.

That makes it a club record sale for City, beating the £82million Atletico Madrid paid for Julian Alvarez in 2024.



City paid Troyes £30.8million for Savio in 2024.

Savio said: “It’s taken a while, but I’m very happy to be here.

“It’s a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

“As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come.

“He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level. And I believe we can do that together, as a team.”



Roberto De Zerbi said: “Savio is a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions.

“He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity. We’re very pleased to have him with us.

“And I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Savio leaves the Etihad with seven goals and 16 assists in 84 games, though he started just seven of his 24 league appearances last season.

Spurs chased him last summer without success, and his arrival takes the club’s spending past £300million this window.

Sports.title: ‘Taste of their own medicine’ – Man Utd fans convinced history will repeat itself if club sign Balde from Barcelona
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans are excited by the prospect of getting one back on Barcelona as they are linked to a loan swoop for Alejandro Balde.

The Red Devils are in the market for a left back this season, and are currently eyeing a number of options.



Luke Shaw needs more support in the position, with the prospect of European competition surely requiring room for rotation in the position.

One name that has recently emerged is that of Barca’s academy star Balde.



While his expected fee of around $45million, as reported by the Athletic, is not something United are looking to spend, there is interest in a one-year loan deal.

The 22-year-old was left out of the squad for their LaLiga opener by Hansi Flick, who said: “I spoke with Balde and told him that, in my opinion, he is not 100 per cent ready. That he should sort out his thoughts, and then we will discuss it.”

Marca report that though La Blaugrana would prefer a permanent move, the late stage of the transfer window could mean they would consider a loan.

The prospect of taking one of the Catalan side’s players on loan has stirred up frustrations in the United fanbase over the Spaniards’ handling of Marcus Rashford‘s loan last season.

The England World Cup star joined the giants on a one-year loan deal with a £26million option to buy, which was snubbed in favour of a £70m move for Newcastle’s Anthony Gordon.

Now United fans have suggested jumping at a Balde loan deal to even the score with Barcelona.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

One fan wrote: “Take Balde on loan, use him for a season, and send him right back to Barcelona. Taste of their own Rashford medicine.”

Another suggested: “IF United are going to go with Balde, it’s time to play Barcelona at their own game. Loan with option to buy. Give them a bit of the Rashford loan treatment.”

The Spanish international is not the only LaLiga target that United are monitoring at left back.

Racing Santander wonderkid Jorge Salinas is another prospect, who is available at a cut price thanks to his €16m release clause.



Atletico Madrid are also understood to be in for the 19-year-old, who could prove a brilliant option for the future if either club pulls the trigger.

Either a cheap deal or a loan agreement could leave the door open for the club to approach Lewis Hall next season.

Michael Carrick and Co are, as it stands, unwilling to meet the considerable price it would take to pry Hall away from Newcastle, with Matthias Jaissle saying on Sunday that there was “no chance” he signs for United this window.

But a loan deal could bring in the required depth while allowing a swoop for Hall on a permanent deal to make financial sense next year.

That particular course of action really would mimic Barcelona’s conduct, replacing their returning loanee with a Newcastle star on a big-money deal.

Sports.title: How many children does Michael Owen have, and what are their names?
Sports.content:
MICHAEL Owen is one of England’s greatest ever strikers, and away from the pitch he’s a father of four.

The Ballon d’Or winner has let cameras into the family home for a new Amazon Prime Video series – here’s everything we know about the Owens.



How many children does Michael Owen have?

Michael Owen has four children with his wife, Louise Bonsall, all of whom feature in new docuseries, Meet the Owens.

Eldest daughter Gemma Rose was born on May 1, 2003, followed by son James Michael on February 6, 2006.



Emily May arrived in October 2007, and youngest daughter Jessica came into the world in February 2010.

Gemma, 23, became a household name in her own right after entering the Love Island villa in 2022, finishing as a runner-up alongside Luca Bish.

She also competed internationally in dressage for Great Britain from the age of 11.

Gemma now works as an influencer with millions of followers on social media, and also runs her own swimwear line.

She still rides horses, and last month, she made her jockey debut in the Magnolia Cup at Glorious Goodwood, finishing fourth on Turbo Trotter from her dad’s Manor House Stables.

She managed the feat just a week after a nasty fall in training left her with minor injuries.



Gemma told Racing TV: “Prep’s been… It’s been intense. Not going to lie, I had a fall a week ago today, and yeah…

“A bit sore, bruises, but nothing’s broken so the show goes on.”

James was diagnosed with Stargardt disease, an inherited condition that destroys central vision and has no cure, at the age of eight.

In 2019, Michael revealed that his son is clinically blind, telling The Times: “He will never be a footballer. My son’s got an eye condition.

“I’ve never said this. I don’t want a big headline. Clinically, he’s blind.



“He’s got Stargardt disease, a degeneration of his retina. I used to go and watch him and bollock him about his positioning.

“He can’t see the ball until it’s five yards away. As much as every father wants their son to play, it is almost a relief to me.

“Everyone always asks, ‘Is he going to be a footballer?’ and then I stand on the side of the pitch and hear, ‘He’s not as good as his dad.’”

James now wants to join the family racing business.



Emily is aiming to become the first Owen to go to university, while Jessica has her sights on becoming an Olympic showjumper.

Gemma became an ambassador for the charity Fight for Sight in 2023, citing her brother’s diagnosis.

Who is Michael Owen’s wife?

Michael is married to childhood sweetheart Louise, who works with horses.

The pair met in primary school in 1984 and became a couple at Hawarden High School in Flintshire, Wales.

He proposed at their home on Valentine’s Day – which is also Louise’s birthday – in 2004, and they married the following year.



In 2004, Louise suffered a serious riding accident and spent three weeks in the Countess of Chester Hospital.

Her back was broken in two places, and her hip and pelvis were also broken in five places.

After the accident, she decided to change her professional focus – instead of training dressage horses, she moved into rehabilitating horses and is an ambassador of the British Thoroughbred Retraining Centre.

What is Meet the Owens about?

The six-part series follows a year in the Owens’ lives, both at home and at Manor House Stables in Cheshire as the family run their racing business.



An insider said: “Michael’s life in horse racing is a world away from his football career and fans will see him swapping big stadiums for stables and all the hard graft that goes with being a racehorse owner.

“All the family is starring in the show, not least Gemma who, since starring on Love Island in 2022, has been balancing life in the public eye as an influencer with over 4million followers alongside her equestrian career, swimwear and brand deals.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s set to be a hilarious and heartfelt look at a family who are juggling ambition and fame in public, as well as navigating a normal family life in private and all that comes with having to live up to a famous name.”

All six episodes land on Amazon Prime Video on Friday, August 28.

Sports.title: Fulham star Josh King admits he has ‘VENDETTA’ against Chelsea after finally banishing controversial strike with goal
Sports.content:
JOSH KING’s “vendetta” against Chelsea wasn’t enough to get an opening day win for Fulham.

But that hasn’t stopped him and his teammates from dreaming of a European place this season.



Fulham’s best young talent netted his side’s equalising goal on Monday after going 1-0 down inside 31 seconds.

It was his second successive season scoring against the Blues, although his last one was controversially disallowed at Stamford Bridge, before then winning Fulham’s Goal of the Month award – and it’s something he is very aware of.



King said: “I don’t know (what it is with me and Chelsea) maybe I had a slight vendetta against them or redemption story going on.

“All I can do is try and contribute, hopefully it won’t be the last this season – I’ll keep working on my finishing and hopefully I’ll score more and more.”



Fulham perhaps shocked a few people with just how much they took the game to Xabi Alonso’s side, and will feel hard done by not to have gotten a point.

After losing their two main goalscorers in Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez, it looked difficult to see them finishing in the top half of the table for most this campaign.

In fact, many are tipping them to either just stay afloat, or even be relegated.

But on Monday nights evidence they will certainly be better than people thought under Alvaro Arbeloa, and King is dreaming of finishing in a European place come May.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He added: “We lost a couple of top finishers in Raul Jimenez and Harry Wilson, so other people have got to step up – I did that today and so did Gonzalo.”

“We’re a team who want to be in those European spots and we want to work hard to get there.

“There is going to be some tough games, Chelsea is one of those, but sometimes it’s not about the three points it’s about how you play.

“I know the quality in our dressing room and how much potential is in our team, and we will show that.”

Sports.title: Joao Pedro laughs off Chelsea’s infamous ‘number nine curse’ as he hails Morgan Rogers impact and Cole Palmer wizardry
Sports.content:
JOAO PEDRO insists he is not bothered by Chelsea’s ‘cursed’ number nine shirt.

The Brazilian took on the new shirt number after being on fire for the Blues in pre-season, and then fired them to a 3-2 win over Fulham with a goal after 31 seconds and an assist for Cole Palmer too – seemingly dispelling any ‘curse’ on his royal blue shirt.



The curse is derived from the fact that the Blues have not had a really successful number nine since Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink – Tammy Abraham and Hernan Crespo have been the best of a bad bunch since him.

Now Pedro, who scored 15 goals in the Premier League last season with the number 20 on his back, doesn’t think he’ll be affected by the ‘curse’.



He smiled: “I just try to do my job. I don’t believe in that.

“Every player is different, and now I have to try to score in every game possible.

“I know my responsibility in the group is to score goals, but I don’t think shirt numbers decide that pressure.”

Pedro carried the mantle for Chelsea last season in terms of goals, but if Monday night is anything to go by, Cole Palmer and new £117 million teammate Morgan Rogers are ready to help lessen the burden on him this season.

All three of them scored against Fulham, with some fans already dubbing them the most frightening attack in the Premier League as most of their rivals fell short on the opening weekend.

Palmer, in particular, looked back to his frightening best after he and Pedro were both left out of their respective World Cup squads and had the summer to rest.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

That, Pedro insisted, was a huge help for him, and so is the signing of Rogers.

He added: “The summer was very good because I didn’t go to help Brazil in the World Cup, so I had a time to recover, relax a bit, and to be ready.

“Cole and Morgan are special players. Everyone knows that.

“I’m very grateful to play with them because I know if I make some runs like I did today, Cole and Morgan are gonna give the ball to me and I have to be ready to score – it’s very special.

“If we move a lot, it will be difficult for defenders to pick us up because they can’t focus on one player. The manager lets us be free on the pitch, and we understand each other well.



“I will enjoy this season with Morgan because I think we can achieve high.”

A squad overhaul, a new manager, and a new system all seemed to help Xabi Alonso’s side – with regularly playing one game a week having most under the impression that they will drastically improve this season.

And Pedro insisted that they are daring to dream of the biggest trophies again with those things in mind.



He ended: “When you play for Chelsea, you always need to look for the biggest trophies, and I think today was a great game to show our power.

“Hopefully we can continue like this in the season.

“Everyone wants to be at Chelsea. It’s a big club, and it’s a pleasure to play here – I’m very happy here.”

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola's behaviour speaks volumes as Liverpool transfer chances emerge
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola's behaviour speaks volumes as Liverpool transfer chances emerge

Liverpool are still trying to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain before this summer transfer window ends, as new head coach Andoni Iraola wants wingers

View 2 Images Liverpool are determined to take Bradley Barcola to Anfield before the transfer window shuts (Image: LOU BENOIST, AFP via Getty Images)

Bradley Barcola and his entourage are not panicking about the length of negotiations between Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain as his transfer saga drags on. It is said they remain confident that both clubs will reach an agreement before the end of this summer transfer window at 11pm on 1 September.

‌



PSG have left Barcola out of the squad for their last two matches. The first was the French Super Cup, which they lost 1-0 to Lens. However, he was photographed training the day beforehand, and also attended the match.

‌



Barcola has not been involved for a fortnight since being an unused substitute in the UEFA Super Cup win over Aston Villa. PSG's only remaining match before the transfer deadline is on Friday night against Lille.

‌



All sides involved in Barcola transfer negotiations appear hopeful that a switch to Liverpool will be finalised during the final days of the summer window. The winger has been linked with the Reds in recent months, however, the process has required patience from all concerned, as several critical elements still need to fall into place.

The initial considerations for Liverpool focused on a genuine willingness to pursue a deal. With Barcola entering the final two years of his Parc des Princes contract, he needed to signal his readiness to leave to force PSG into a decision.

Liverpool then needed to establish themselves as the leading contenders to land Barcola, which happened swiftly, before PSG set about identifying replacements in the transfer market to bolster their own attacking ranks. Everything fell into place for the Reds, who then faced the most daunting hurdle of all: club-to-club negotiations.

Les Parisiens placed a hefty price tag on the winger, creating a significant gap between the two clubs that needed to be closed before any deal could be struck. PSG knocked back initial bids as Liverpool looked to formalise their interest, with talks continuing deep into the final week of the transfer window.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It now appears the drawn-out saga is at last moving towards a conclusion that works for all involved, with widespread expectation that Barcola will ultimately complete his move to Anfield. According to a report from L'Equipe, Liverpool are readying a final bid for the winger that they are confident PSG will accept, following a narrowing of the valuation gap between the two clubs over recent weeks.

It is understood that Barcola and his representatives are growing increasingly optimistic that a deal will be struck, with 'nobody in panic mode', despite the apparent lack of progress thus far. There is an expectation that the transfer fee will exceed the Ligue Un record for a sale to a foreign club, surpassing both Ayyoub Bouaddi's impending switch to Manchester City this summer and Neymar's move to Al-Hilal in 2023.

‌



The exact final sum remains unclear, with those details to be finalised in the dying days of the summer transfer window. Nevertheless, the deal would significantly strengthen Liverpool's attacking arsenal.

This marks just one of multiple expected transactions in Liverpool's late transfer flurry, with attention still focused on Minteh to bolster the right-wing choices at Andoni Iraola's disposal. Meanwhile, Cody Gakpo remains the subject of rumours regarding a potential exit. All of which suggests a frantic final week in the market for the Reds, with substantial business to be completed both incoming and outgoing at the club.

Sports.title: Joao Pedro predicts trophies for Chelsea thanks to 'very special' attacking weapons
Sports.content:
Joao Pedro predicts trophies for Chelsea thanks to 'very special' attacking weapons

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League campaign under Xabi Alonso with a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, with Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers all scoring

View 2 Images Chelsea put Fulham to the sword at Craven Cottage (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

Joao Pedro believes Chelsea’s deadly trio will leave Premier League defenders chasing shadows this season.

‌



Chelsea forwards Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were all on target in their first win of the season at Fulham to send out a clear title warning to the rest. They have got big trophies in their sights under new boss Xabi Alonso and Chelsea might just have the best forward line in the top flight.

‌



Brazil star Pedro believes their movement, understanding and goals will make them “very special” and incredibly difficult to stop.

‌



He said: “Cole and Morgan are special players. Everyone knows that. I'm very grateful to play with them because I know if I make some runs, if you know Cole, Morgan's going to give the ball to me and I have to be ready to score. So it's very special.

“I think now in the game, if we move a lot, it will be difficult for defenders to pick up one player to stay. And the manager let us be free on the pitch, so we understand each other well. I think this helps us, and hopefully, it can happen more times.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“When you play for Chelsea, you always need to look for that (the biggest trophies), and I think we’ve already had a great game to show our power and hopefully we can continue like this in the season.”

Chelsea boss Alonso clearly has a turbo-charged front three because Pedro and Palmer had the summer off after not making the Brazil and England squads respectively. Rogers is the club’s £117m British record transfer buy and looks energized after England’s World Cup campaign.

‌



They have been marked down by many pundits as potential challengers to champions Arsenal as they have an elite manager and, with no European football, time to work in training as well as extra rest.

Pedro believes Rogers will be a huge addition to the squad while they are also relishing the chance to work under Alonso. He said: “The summer was very good because I didn't go to Brazil squad in the World Cup, so I had a time to recover myself, relax a bit, to be ready.

View 2 Images Joao Pedro lifted home a brilliant opener after just 30 seconds against Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“I think we need to go step by step. We have to focus on the Premier League and the cups. We have a lot of time to train as well to know what the coach wants from us. I think everyone wants to be at Chelsea. It's a big club. It's a pleasure to play here, and I'm very happy here. I will enjoy this season with Morgan because I think we can achieve high.

“I know Morgan from a long time ago because we played against each other. So when he joined the club, I knew. It was very good for us because he's a very good player, and I think he can help us like he has already.”

Pedro has also taken the No9 shirt this season which is a big thing for Chelsea fans because they have seen so many big names fail wearing that in the past. Mateja Kezman, Hernan Crespo, Fernando Torres, Radamel Falcao, Alvaro Morata, Gonzalo Higuain, Tammy Abraham, Romelu Lukaku, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Liam Delap have all worn it in the past and struggled.

Article continues below

But Pedro insists he has no fears about it - and is relishing the chance to score a lot of goals this season after getting off to a good start. He added: “I just try to do my job. I don't believe in that. Every player is different. I think now I know my responsibility in the group, but I don't think numbers can decide this pressure.

“I just try to enjoy and try to help my team every game. Any day of the season, see what I get. I think I just try to score every opportunity I have.”

Sports.title: Liverpool will ignore Jamie Carragher's desperate transfer plea with focus elsewhere
Sports.content:
Liverpool will ignore Jamie Carragher's desperate transfer plea with focus elsewhere

Liverpool are prioritising the signing of attacking wide players in the final few days of the summer transfer window, much to the annoyance of Jamie Carragher

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher wants a new midfielder at Liverpool (Image: Sky Sports)

Liverpool will not sign a central midfielder in the final few days of the summer transfer window, despite a passionate plea from Jamie Carragher.

‌



The Reds kicked off their Premier League campaign with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Sunday. Dominik Szoboszlai's last-gasp penalty earned Andoni Iraola's side a point after conceding to Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock.

‌



Iraola fielded Szoboszlai in midfield alongside Ryan Gravenberch at St James' Park, with Alexis Mac Allister coming off the bench in the second half. Carragher was alarmed by how open the away side were on the break, with Newcastle ripping through Liverpool's defences with their pace.

‌



Liverpool have so far brought in defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo and winger Victor Munoz this summer. They are now chasing Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola before the window closes on September 1.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The Athletic reports that, despite selling Curtis Jones to Inter Milan for £25.7million plus £4.3m in add-ons, they are not planning to bring in another midfielder. Academy graduate Trey Nyoni, 19, is considered ready to step up and add to his 20 first-team appearances.

Fellow midfielder James McConnell could be sent out on loan to the Championship to further reduce numbers in the middle of the pitch, where Wataru Endo is also available.

After tearing apart Liverpool's midfield, and particularly Gravenberch for his failure to track Willock for Newcastle's second goal, Carragher made his feelings clear on Sky Sports.

‌



View 2 Images Ryan Gravenberch's performance against Newcastle was criticised by Jamie Carragher (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

He said: “Liverpool need someone alongside Gravenberch. It doesn't necessarily need to be a player who can't get on the ball and he's just tackling and stopping players. If you play for one of the top teams in the world, you need to be able to get hold of the ball.

“But I want someone who can run. Szoboszlai has to go to the No 10. I've always seen this coming. When people are saying [Wirtz] has got to go to No 10, that means Szoboszlai's got to be in the team and he's not a central midfield player.

‌



“I thought this would come up in six weeks, I think it's coming up right now. I don't see where he fits in at all, really. What's Iraola going to do with Wirtz? You can't keep going with it; it's not working,

“It didn't work last season. Liverpool last season conceded 78 goals, 53 in the Premier League, the most they've ever conceded in the Premier League. And all of a sudden it's all about buying wingers?"

Sports.title: Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates

Bruno Fernandes has so often been the hero for Manchester United, but the Reds skipper has been the subject of ire from club icon Paul Scholes

View 3 Images Paul Scholes was not happy with Bruno Fernandes' recent comments (Image: YouTube/The Good, the Bad and the Football podcast)

Bruno Fernandes has been told to "shut his mouth" by Paul Scholes after the Manchester United skipper criticised his team-mates. Fernandes blasted United for repeating the clumsy errors they repeatedly made last season after their 2-0 defeat to Hull City.

‌



The shock result was only Michael Carrick's second Premier League defeat as United manager, but there is already an inquisition about the Reds' transfer business. They spent £85million on midfield duo Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, who were both hauled off in the second half as United looked for a route back into the game.

‌



After Fernandes' cutting honesty about how he and his team-mates played against Hull, Scholes expressed his unhappiness with the Portuguese ace's comments.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When quizzed about the United captain's criticism, Scholes, speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, said: "When you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut, because he didn't have his best performance either."

Following the defeat to the relegation favourites, Fernandes told TNT Sports: "Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

‌



"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these type of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.

View 3 Images Fernandes' comments were not received well by Paul Scholes (Image: PAUL ELLIS, AFP via Getty Images)

"We knew before the game set-pieces would be a big part of their game. They played all pre-season with a back four but had a five against us for some height, for these moments. The most frustrating thing is that we lost the game."

‌



Fernandes slotted alongside Tielemans and Santos in United's midfield, which endured a torrid afternoon against the Tigers. Reflecting on the outcome, Scholes does not believe any of the new additions have been an upgrade, stating: "You speak about recruitment wise and I saw the central midfield the other day and I thought 'that is no better than last'.

"I mean, when you're recruiting players and looking for a different team, you think, 'I've got to get better.' To me, on Saturday, that wasn't better than Kobbie Mainoo and Casemiro together."

View 3 Images Hull were by far the better team against United (Image: George Wood, Getty Images)

‌



United are hopeful of shortly unveiling Carlos Baleba as their latest signing. The Brighton & Hove Albion star appears set to become the third central midfielder to arrive at the club this campaign.

Baleba is anticipated to complete a £70m switch to United, which would push the Reds' total spending on central midfielders to £135m. United welcome Ipswich Town to Old Trafford in their next Premier League outing on Sunday, August 30.

Sports.title: Chelsea braced for new Enzo Fernandez bid from Man City 11 days after deadline
Sports.content:
Chelsea braced for new Enzo Fernandez bid from Man City 11 days after deadline

Enzo Fernandez could leave Chelsea for a reunion with Enzo Maresca at Manchester City in the final stages of the summer transfer window after being booed on Monday

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso could lose Enzo Fernandez in the coming days (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Chelsea are braced for Manchester City to make a fresh bid for Enzo Fernandez.

‌



Argentina star Fernandez’s future has been uncertain this summer as he became a target for new City boss Enzo Maresca. Chelsea set a strict deadline for clubs to meet their £120million price on August 14 - and that has now long since passed.

‌



It remains to be seen whether City will make a formal bid and if that gets any encouragement, but Chelsea have made their position clear that they did not want to sell. But it is believed there could be one last attempt by City to get Fernandez as the Chelsea midfielder has been unsettled at the club since being axed last season for flirting with Real Madrid.

‌



Fernandez got heavily booed by Fulham fans in his first appearance in the Premier League as a substitute on Monday night. That was a reaction to Fernandez’s part in Argentina’s bad tempered win over England in the World Cup semi-final.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

But, interestingly, Chelsea fans sang his name and Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso also made it clear he wants clarity over Fernandez’s future this week.

‌



Alonso told BBC Radio 5Live: “In football, I am not surprised by anything. We will see. My wish is that we know what will happen for the future but we will see this week.”

The transfer window will shut at 11pm BST on Tuesday, September 1.

Manchester City have already splashed out £116m on Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest but are in need of reinforcements in central midfield. Maresca fielded defender Marc Guehi in midfield in their 2-1 win over Bournemouth, which saw six defenders named in the starting XI.

‌



View 2 Images Enzo Maresca wants a reunion with Enzo Fernandez (Image: Getty Images)

Anderson, Matteo Kovacic and Mateus Nunes could soon be the only specialist options available, with Nico Gonzalez heading to Newcastle for around £50m. They have just sold Rodri to Barcelona for £65m and Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah for £52m, meaning there is plenty of cash available.

Maresca coached Fernandez at Chelsea, but refused to be drawn on the possible deal. He said: "In this moment I have to give you the same answer since day one, which will be always the same. He is a player from another club and I don't think it's correct to talk about other players.

Article continues below

"I'm not going to say anything about players who are not with us. Not today, to be honest. I don't think we're going to do something today."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso's four-word message to Robert Sanchez after Chelsea goalkeeper's nightmare
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso's four-word message to Robert Sanchez after Chelsea goalkeeper's nightmare

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League campaign - and the Xabi Alonso era - with a 3-2 win over Fulham, but Robert Sanchez's performance in goal left a lot to be desired

View 2 Images Robert Sanchez was arguably at fault for both Fulham goals (Image: AFP / Getty Images)

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has encouraged Robert Sanchez to "relax and carry on" despite his dreadful start to the Premier League season.

‌



The Blues picked up a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, with Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers all scoring at Craven Cottage. But while their attack looked impressive, there was an obvious issue at the other end.

‌



Sanchez was beaten at his near post by Josh King's low effort and he was also at fault for Fulham's second goal, pushing out a shot for Gonzalo Garcia to head in a rebound.

‌



The Spanish goalkeeper's erratic performances are nothing new, with mistakes a feature of his three-year Chelsea career. But Alonso refused to criticise his goalkeeper when speaking to reporters post-match.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's about the team, it's not about the individual," Alonso said when asked about Sanchez's mistakes. "The first goal, we can do better to defend, we can do better to avoid, but it's part of the game. We need to accept and to learn. This is going to be a process.

"All the lines, from the strikers, the midfielders, the defence, the goalkeepers, we want to do better in everything. The goal was to start good, and we've been able to start well. Relax and carry on."

Sanchez has been Chelsea's number one goalkeeper since joining for £20million from Brighton three years ago. He has made 112 appearances, keeping his place in the side in spite of Chelsea's busy nature in the transfer market.

‌



View 2 Images Xabi Alonso dismissed concerns about his goalkeeper (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

Mike Penders, a 21-year-old goalkeeper who has never made an appearance for Chelsea, was on the bench against Fulham. The Belgian joined last summer from Genk and spent last season on loan at sister club Strasbourg. Filip Jorgensen, who was the back-up last season, has been sent to Strasbourg on loan for the 2026/27 season.

Both Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville have urged Chelsea to sign a new goalkeeper before the transfer window closes on September 1 to replace Sanchez.

‌



"I do think [there are] concerns defensively," Carragher said on Sky Sports after the Fulham game. "They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it's going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight."

Neville added: "I don't know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It's a problem."

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher make Premier League predictions with shock relegation candidate
Sports.content:
Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher make Premier League predictions with shock relegation candidate

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have named their picks for the title, top four and relegation, with the Sky Sports pundits struggling to agree on much after the opening weekend

View 4 Images Gary Neville has disagreed with Jamie Carragher with his choices (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have given their full predictions for the Premier League season - and while they both agree Arsenal will win the title, there is little consensus elsewhere.

‌



The first weekend of the Premier League campaign has been and gone, with Manchester United and Tottenham suffering heavy defeats at the hands of Hull and Brentford respectively. Arsenal kicked off their title defence with a convincing win over Coventry while Manchester City came from behind to beat Bournemouth.

‌



Liverpool snatched a late point in a 2-2 draw at Newcastle before Chelsea overcame Fulham in an entertaining 3-2 victory on Monday night.

‌



We have now seen every side play and there is now less than a week remaining in the summer transfer window for teams to bolster their squads. It means prediction time for Sky Sports pundits Neville and Carragher, who have opened themselves up to embarrassment by sharing their calls.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



There are no surprises for the title, with both ex-players tipping Arsenal for a second consecutive title. "They're way out in front," according to Neville. But the two cannot agree on the remainder of the top places.

Neville feels that Chelsea's summer recruitment and the arrival of Xabi Alonso can push them up from 10th place last season to second this time around. "Just purely because of the fact that they've got no European football," he explained. "If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they're only playing 45 games, they're going to amass an enormous amount of points.

"That's based upon the fact that they're going to have more free weeks, they're not going to have the injury pressures, they're not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that. I think they'll just edge past Manchester City."

‌



View 4 Images Jamie Carragher has tipped Sunderland for relegation (Image: YouTube/The Overlap)

In typical Carragher-Neville fashion, both is tipping their ex-club to finish about the other's in fourth place. "I can't separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea," Neville said. "I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth."

Carragher said: "I think Liverpool would want more, but I think just looking at the Chelsea situation, Liverpool where they are right now, I don't see any way they'd be in the top two, and I don't see any way they can mount a title challenge."

‌



At the other end of the table, Carragher has surprisingly tipped Sunderland to get relegated. The Black Cats finished seventh in their first campaign back in the top flight last season to earn a place in the Europa League - and that could cost them.

View 4 Images Arsenal won their first Premier League title in 22 years in May (Image: Getty)

"The fact that they've got European football, they're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday," Carragher explained. "I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder, where they came up and had a really brilliant season, finished high up the table but a lot of the games, like Sunderland, you win by the odd goal. I'm not saying it's luck but their underlying numbers had them not far away from relegation."

‌



Meanwhile, Neville has picked the three promoted sides - Hull, Coventry and Ipswich - to go straight back down, but feels that Fulham under Alvaro Arbeloa could also be in trouble.

Sports.title: Baumgardner to face undefeated Turhan as blockbuster Dubois showdown nears
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Caroline Dubois a step closer.

Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.

"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

"I do not want to lose either. As two boxers sharing a 'win at all costs' mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight and only one winner."

Victory for Baumgardner would see her become a two-weight world champion in the same division as Dubois, who holds the WBC and WBO titles.

The 32-year-old is set to be ringside for Dubois' clash with Amelia Moore on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Since December, Dubois has been vociferous in calling out Baumgardner, and those calls have only intensified since she beat Terri Harper to unify the division in April.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Baumgardner dismissed the prospects of facing Caroline Dubois after her win over Bo Mi Re Shin. Instead, the fighter called out Katie Taylor and Amanda Serrano

Baumgardner has maintained that, despite her status as a unified world champion, Dubois has yet to reach the level required for her to entertain a fight between them.

But should Baumgardner inflict a first career defeat on Turhan, all roads will surely lead to a blockbuster unification bout with Dubois, where the winner would move to within one victory of becoming undisputed champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dubois is determined to fight Baumgardner sooner rather than later

The co-main event on November 8 will see England's Ellie Scotney fight the undefeated Tiara Brown over 10 rounds for the WBC featherweight world title.

Former undisputed super bantamweight champion Scotney will step up to 126lbs as she bids to become a two-weight world champion.

"MVPW-07 is one of the biggest championship events in boxing history, with four back-to-back world title fights, bringing together eight elite fighters from around the world with belts at stake in every match-up," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.
