A group of Polish civil society organisations has urged a former government minister to withdraw his candidacy to become a Constitutional Tribunal (TK) judge, saying his close ties to the prime minister could undermine confidence in the court’s independence. In a joint statement, the nine organisations say that restoring the legitimacy of the court, which has been in crisis since 2015 following illegitimate judicial appointments made by the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, requires not only addressing legal irregularities but also rebuilding public trust. “The existence of the Constitutional Tribunal as an organ of judicial power only makes sense if it is an independent arbiter,” they say. 🔴Wspólnie z innymi organizacjami apelujemy do dr. M. Berka o rezygnację z kandydowania do TK, a do Sejmu o wybór osoby niezależnej politycznie. Droga do praworządności to nie „odbijanie” Trybunału, ale odbudowa jego autorytetu. Przeczytajcie nasz apel, link w komentarzu ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/LPlbk39lNr — Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka (@hfhrpl) August 20, 2026 The appeal follows Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s announcement that Maciej Berek, who until recently served as a government minister and whom Tusk has described as his “right-hand man”, would be put forward as a candidate for the Constitutional Tribunal. The choice has drawn particular attention because Tusk came to power promising to “depoliticise” the court after the previous PiS government appointed former politicians as judges. “Regardless of the extent to which the tribunal has become politicised, the way to reform this institution cannot be for it to be ‘recaptured’ or ‘taken over’ by another ruling majority,” the NGOs write in the statement. The organisations, including the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights, the Institute of Public Affairs and the Stefan Batory Foundation, say Berek’s close ties to the current political leadership could cause his appointment to be perceived as political, regardless of his legal qualifications or personal integrity. “Not only must courts and tribunals operate independently and impartially, but citizens must also recognise and have confidence in that independence and impartiality. This is not possible when judges are appointed whose links to the government are immediately apparent,” the organisations add. “We therefore call on Dr Maciej Berek to withdraw his candidacy in the interests of the independence of the constitutional judiciary.” The proportion of Poles who negatively assess the justice system has increased under the current government, despite its promises to restore the rule of law. State pollster @CBOS_Info found 61% now hold a negative view, up from 55% in 2022 and 51% in 2017 https://t.co/P3fbTTbS5C — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 12, 2026 The organisations also argue that Berek’s nomination goes against a principle that the current ruling coalition sought to introduce: that anyone who has held political office within the previous four years should be barred from appointment to the tribunal. Berek was a government minister until last week. The coalition’s proposal was included in a bill approved by parliament in 2024. However, the Constitutional Tribunal itself later ruled the provision unconstitutional after former President Andrzej Duda, an ally of PiS, referred the legislation for review. “Although this law has not come into force, it would be reasonable for the Sejm to adhere to the standard it has adopted,” they said, referring to the lower chamber of the parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 However, the selection of Berek, whose candidacy was put forward by MPs from Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO), has exposed divisions within the ruling coalition, which ranges from centre-right to left. “We were supposed to be different from PiS; we were supposed to do things differently, not exactly the same way,” Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, told Polsat News. Paweł Śliz, leader of the centre-right Poland 2050’s (Polska 2050) caucus, said Berek would make an excellent Constitutional Tribunal judge were it not for his recent role as a government minister. “I consider him an excellent, outstanding professional; I value his experience and expertise. However, my position on this matter is unequivocal. I will not compromise my principles,” he told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The chief justice of the constitutional court has refused to accept four new judges appointed by parliament but whom the opposition-aligned president has refused to swear in. The decision deepens an unprecedented standoff over Poland's top court https://t.co/B02DKA3uBL — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 9, 2026 Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition opposing Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. Last week, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Presidential spokesman Rafał Leśkiewicz told PAP on Thursday that “there are serious doubts” about Berek’s formal qualifications to become a Constitutional Tribunal judge. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has summoned Israel’s ambassador to express its “great disappointment” that the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) have discontinued an investigation into the strikes on an aid convoy in Gaza in 2024 that killed seven humanitarian workers, including a Pole, Damian Soból. “Partnership requires mutual respect,” declared foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, as well as the failure of accountability for [the] IDF’s excessive use of force[,] are undermining public support in even pro-Israel nations.” Partnership requires mutual respect. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, as well as the failure of accountability for IDF’s excessive use of force are undermining public support in even pro-Israel nations. https://t.co/9H0nhiDE4H — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) August 20, 2026 The incident in question took place in April 2024, when Israeli drones struck a convoy delivering humanitarian aid from World Central Kitchen (WCK), a major international food relief NGO. The attack killed seven aid workers, including Soból. The incident caused outrage in Poland, whose government demanded that Israel fully explain the circumstances. The IDF expressed “sincere sorrow” over the deaths and pledged to carry out a “thorough and transparent” investigation. On Wednesday this week, the IDF announced that it had closed the case after determining “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct that would justify the opening of a criminal investigation or the taking of additional measures against any of those involved in the incident”. The IDF said that its troops had identified a gunman on one of the trucks in the convoy. It also claimed that WCK had hired an armed security force to protect the convoy without coordinating that with IDF authorities and that the convoy deviated from the route previously agreed with the IDF. However, the IDF also acknowledged that it had mistakenly identified several individuals as being armed. It added that attempts to contact WCK representatives over a half-hour period while the convoy was on the move were unsuccessful. The IDF noted that, after the incident, two military officers were removed from their positions while three others were reprimanded. But it found that there was no basis for any further action. ⚖️ IDF prosecution rules on five FFAM cases: The IDF says its General Staff Fact-Finding and Assessment Mechanism has completed reviews of approximately 150 exceptional wartime incidents since the beginning of the war and transferred them to the Military Prosecution. Decisions… pic.twitter.com/H5g4qOu5e2 — Israel Realtime (@IsraelRealtime) August 19, 2026 On Thursday, Poland’s foreign ministry issued a statement saying that it was “greatly disappointed to receive the information provided about the discontinuation of the proceedings by the Israeli military authorities”. It announced that it had summoned the Israeli ambassador in order to “communicate a critical assessment of the actions taken to date to clarify the causes and course of the tragedy”. It also noted that Polish prosecutors are still conducting their own investigation and that the foreign ministry had informed the Israeli ambassador that they “expect the Israeli side will provide the relevant Polish authorities with all necessary explanations and materials requested”. “The circumstances of the tragedy should be fully investigated and [we] do not accept that the perpetrators are avoiding legal and moral responsibility,” concluded the ministry, adding that “the families deserve adequate compensation”. We strongly condemn the Israeli military prosecutor’s account of the deaths of our seven colleagues on April 1, 2024. And we fundamentally disagree with their decision about criminal investigations into the IDF airstrikes that killed our team. Read our full statement here:… — World Central Kitchen (@WCKitchen) August 19, 2026 The IDF’s findings were also condemned by WCK itself, which called them “inconsistent with the full truth and deeply offensive”. It added that, “at the time of the lethal attacks, the IDF knew that our team in Gaza was unarmed and posing a threat to nobody”. The NGO repeated its demand for an independent investigation into the incident, “because the IDF cannot credibly investigate its own conduct”. On Friday, the UK, Canada and Australia, whose citizens were also killed in the strike, issued a joint statement calling the IDF’s decision to drop the investigation “shameful” and another example of the lack of accountability for incidents in Gaza. Joint statement from the foreign ministries of Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom on Israel closing the investigation into strikes on the World Central Kitchen convoy in Gaza on 1 April 2024 ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/V3CZe286tN — Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (@FCDOGovUK) August 21, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Main image credit: World Central Kitchen

World.title: New official tasked with promoting Poland criticised over error-strewn, potentially AI-generated report
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A government official appointed last month to promote Poland abroad has been hit by a wave of criticism after it emerged that she authored a report containing errors and which shows signs of being generated by artificial intelligence. The document mislocated major Polish cities and included bizarre language mixing Polish and English. It was marked as being part of a project financed by the sport and tourism ministry, though the ministry itself has denied that claim. The opposition has called on prosecutors to investigate potential misuse of public funds. ⁉️ Czy “Markę Polska” ma nam wygenerować sztuczna inteligencja? ⁉️ Czy Ministerstwo Sportu i Turystyki zapłaciło 200 000 złotych w ramach zadania publicznego za raport wygenerowany przez AI? ⁉️ Czy mogę prosić Panią Minister prof. @b_mroz_gorgon o odniesienie się do tych pytań… pic.twitter.com/lM2AY88oAh — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 The official in question, Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, is a professor at Wrocław University of Economics who was appointed three weeks ago as the government’s plenipotentiary for the promotion of Poland’s brand, a newly created position. She was presented at a press conference by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. However, this week, journalists and commentators began highlighting cases of bizarre errors from a report, titled A Self-Portrait of the Poles (Polaków Portret Własny), published last year with Mróz-Gorgoń named as the author, in her position as president of a think tank called Marka Polska (Brand Poland). The report contained some glaring errors, such as describing the city of Katowice as being in “north central” Poland (whereas in fact it is in the south) and Wrocław as being in the “northwest” (when it is actually in the southwest). Geografia – czyli gdzie leżą Katowice A propos miast jest też ciekawy chochlik lub też, jakby to powiedział ktoś złośliwy, klasyczna halucynacja AI. Przy opisie badań FGI miasta opisane są w następujący sposób (zdjęcie poniżej): 👉 Olsztyn – północny wschód 👉 Szczecin -… pic.twitter.com/SF6XBRfhWS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 Other parts contain strange analysis, such as noting that “after World War Two, Germany did not build its brand on the Holocaust”. The text also features unusual language, including random use of words in English, some of which have been turned into Polish ones. It is also regularly features words written in capital letters. One sentence, for example, refers to “INSTABILNOŚĆ” and “REZILIENCE”, presumably meaning “instability” and “resilience”, but neither of which is a Polish word. Another section claims that 95% of Poles born after 1990 are “polilingwalni” (an invented Polonised version of “polylingual”) who speak “angielski fluent”, a strange linguistic mix that means they speak English fluently. As well as the unusual language, the very claim that 95% of young Poles speak fluent English, as well as that many additionally speak Mandarin, has been questioned by many commentators. The report also contains bizarre errors in footnotes, which are numbered randomly (on one page, three consecutive footnotes are numbered “41, 517, 6”) and some of which are completely empty. A number of expert commentators have suggested that the text contains clear indications that it was generated by AI, a claim supported by evidence from programmes that check texts for AI-generated content. AI czy nie AI, oto jest pytanie Czytając ten raport kilkukrotnie, trudno mi było pozbyć się wrażenia, że nikt poważny, a szczególnie naukowiec z tytułem doktora habilitowanego, nie wygenerowałby dużych części raportu, za który zapłacili podatnicy, w jakimś LLM. No bo przecież… pic.twitter.com/jyTexgmeXS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 As well as bearing Mróz-Gorgoń’s name as author, the report also features on its front cover the logo of the sport and tourism ministry. The first page then includes a note saying that the project was carried out under an initiative co-financed by the ministry. After the issue began to draw attention and criticism on Thursday, the ministry issued a statement saying that the report was not ordered by them, was not part of any agreement to which the ministry was a party, and that no request to use the ministry’s logo was submitted. However, a social media post last November by deputy sport and tourism minister Piotr Borys shows him attending an event to present the report. He thanked Mróz-Gorgoń for coordinating the project and inviting him to the presentation. 📚W Akademii Leona Koźmińskiego odbyła się prezentacja raportu „Polaków Portret Własny”, przygotowanego Think Tank Marka Polska. To wyjątkowe wydarzenie poświęcone premierze badań dotyczących DNA Marki Polska. 🧬To pierwsze tak kompleksowe badanie, które pokazuje, kim jesteśmy… pic.twitter.com/jb7KdCJTPM — Piotr Borys (@piotr_borys) November 26, 2025 On Thursday evening, Mróz-Gorgoń herself addressed the controversy in an interview with Polsat News. She said that the report was actually a “work in progress” that “should never have appeared in the public space”. However, she still defended the work, saying that “the research was conducted reliably” and “the conclusions stand up to scrutiny”. But she also admitted that the writing of the report had been “aided by artificial intelligence”. In separate remarks to the Polish Press Agency (PAP), she said that “we used AI tools solely for transcription, summarising and text editing; they did not design research content or draw conclusions…We worked according to social science methodology, diligently and without cutting corners”. Meanwhile, on the Marka Polska think tank’s website, where the report had been published, it was initially changed on Thursday to being marked as a “draft version” before later being deleted entirely. Od raportu i deklaracji, że “praca badawcza [została] przeprowadzona zgodnie z zasadami nauk społecznych, rzetelnie i merytorycznie, w oparciu o opisaną metodologię”, przez “work in progress”, aż do “Oops! That page can’t be found”. PiS has also called on Mróz-Gorgoń to resign or to be fired. On Friday, a deputy digital affairs minister, Dariusz Standerski, told the Wirtualna Polska news website that “all the circumstances surrounding the creation of this report will be clarified”. The controversy around Mróz-Gorgoń comes just days after the sport and tourism ministry was involved in the launch of a new advertising campaign designed to encourage tourism to Poland, but which many commentators have argued was poorly conceived and executed. World.title: ASEAN Plus Three Film Festival Returns to Prague for Its Fifth Edition
World.content:
The ASEAN Committee in Prague (ACP), representing the embassies of ASEAN member states, together with the embassies of China, Japan and the Republic of Korea, will host the fifth edition of the ASEAN Plus Three Film Festival (APTFF).

The festival will begin on Monday, September 7, 2026, at the Municipal Library of Prague.

Organised in cooperation with the Municipal Library of Prague, the festival will run until September 14 and feature seven full-length films, alongside a curated selection of short films from across the ASEAN Plus Three region.



Since its launch in 2022, the APTFF has introduced Czech audiences to the diverse cultures and cinematic voices of ASEAN and its Plus Three partners.

Previous editions have featured acclaimed films including Escape from Mogadishu (Republic of Korea), Father and Son (Viet Nam) and Yuni (Indonesia).

This year’s programme includes Solata: Friends Are the Family We Choose (Indonesia), Babah (Malaysia), The Beginning (Myanmar), I’m Perfect (the Philippines), 4 Tigers (Thailand), Song of the South (Viet Nam) and One and Only (China).

A selection of short films will also be screened during the opening night on September 7.

The programme includes Mbiyodo/Communal Work (Indonesia), Ninavau (Malaysia), Myanmar Be Enchanted (Myanmar), Lola Loleng/Grandma Loleng (the Philippines), Give to Getters (Thailand), Welcome to Viet Nam (Viet Nam), My Chinese Ecological Notes (China), Pukkulapottas and Hours in the Forest (Japan), and Persona (Republic of Korea).

Beyond its cultural programme, the festival is part of a broader effort by ASEAN and its Plus Three partners to introduce Czech audiences to the region, its societies and creative industries, as well as its shared identity as a community of more than 690 million people.

All screenings are open to the public and free of charge. Films will be shown in their original languages with English and Czech subtitles.

The full programme and schedule are available on the Municipal Library of Prague website.

World.title: GALLERY: Light Installation “Synapse” Coming to Florenc Metro Station
World.content:
Jan Poš light installation Synapse will go on display in the Florenc Line C metro passage at the end of September.

The artwork will track passengers’ movements and complement the existing Battle of Sokolovo mosaic. Prague city councillors approved around CZK 1.38 million in funding to complete and install the artwork.

“Synapse” is a light-based installation by visual artist Jan Poš (1996) and the winning entry in the “Light for the Metro” competition held in 2023.



The aim was to create a light artwork for the passage connecting the north and south concourses of Florenc metro station. A total of 23 artists and teams submitted proposals, with four advancing to the final stage, which was conducted as a competitive dialogue.

The five-member jury considered the artwork’s long-term maintenance and its ability to withstand demanding operating conditions.

According to Poš, the artwork, installed on the wall opposite the underpass’s main staircase, comes into view as metro passengers ascend or descend the stairs.

It becomes part of their daily journey while remaining elegantly set apart, creating a space where it can stand on its own and offer a moment of respite from the hustle and bustle.

Poš says the work’s format and style enliven and build on the Battle of Sokolovo mosaic, creating a bridge between the past and present of the city.

The artwork was originally due to be installed alongside the completion of the reconstruction of the station’s ceiling slab. Prague’s public transport operator, DPP, has been repairing the structure since 2022 due to corrosion.

World.title: Partial Lunar Eclipse to Be Visible From Prague at Dawn on August 28
World.content:
Prague residents willing to get up early on Friday, August 28, will have a chance to witness a partial lunar eclipse, with almost the entire Moon passing into Earth’s shadow shortly before it sets.

The eclipse will reach its maximum at 6:12 a.m. CEST. By then, only a narrow section along the Moon’s northern edge will remain illuminated.

In Prague, the Moon is expected to set at approximately 6:17 a.m., leaving only a few minutes to observe the eclipse at its peak.



The partial phase will begin at 4:33 a.m. As the event progresses, Earth’s shadow will gradually cover the lunar surface, reducing the bright portion of the Moon until only a thin illuminated crescent remains visible.

Astronomers at the Silesian University in Opava say observers will need an unobstructed view towards the southwest, as the Moon will be low above the horizon throughout the most important part of the event.

The eclipse follows another major astronomical event visible from the Czech Republic earlier this month, giving skywatchers a second opportunity to observe a rare celestial phenomenon within a short period.

Unlike a solar eclipse, observing the Moon does not require protective eyewear. The eclipse can be seen with the naked eye, while binoculars or a camera may provide a closer view.

For the best chance of seeing the maximum phase, observers should choose a location with a clear southwestern horizon and arrive before dawn. Weather conditions will also play a decisive role in whether the eclipse is visible.

World.title: September 19: Prague Hosts Indian Festival of Music, Food, and Community
World.content:
Prague will host its annual celebration of Indian culture, Ganeshotsav, on Saturday, September 19, at Kulturní dům Ládví.

Ganeshotsav, the festival honoring Lord Ganesha, is more than a celebration of Indian culture—it’s a way to bring people together.

Since 2021, the festival has grown into a space where Indian and Czech communities can meet, connect, and enjoy shared traditions.

The event is organised by Maharashtra Mandal, Czech Republic, a registered non-profit dedicated to promoting friendship and understanding between Indian and Czech residents.

The festival features traditional Indian rituals, music, dance, and food, and welcomes everyone to join in the fun.

Like last year, this year, the festival adds a charitable aspect: part of the registration fees will go to support non-profits in the Czech Republic.

“With this initiative, we want to contribute to the development of communities both in our country of origin and in the country that is now our home,” says the organizers to Prague Morning.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Maharashtra Mandal Czech Republic (@maharashtramandalczechrepublic)

By partnering with like-minded organisations, the festival encourages intercultural dialogue, mutual respect, and connections between diverse communities living in the Czech Republic.

Like last year, organizers will support small entrepreneurs from the Indian community who will present the diversity of Indian cuisine.

The project is called “”Our Annapoorna -The Taste of Every Indian Household”, and will offer visitors a diverse selection of traditional dishes from different corners of India.

The cultural program, featuring music, dance, and traditional rituals, will run from 5:00 PM to 8:30 PM

World.title: A Multi-Brand K-Beauty Pop-Up Is Coming to Prague This September
World.content:
A Korean beauty pop-up will bring eight K-beauty brands and K-pop entertainment to Prague’s Vltava River this September.

The HARUNARU K-Beauty Pop-up will take place aboard KVASOUL, a self-brewing boat restaurant, from September 4 to 8.



An industry preview for beauty professionals and influencers will be held on September 3.

Visitors will be able to discover, test and buy products from eight Korean brands, including GASH, ranked No. 1 at Olive Young, South Korea’s leading beauty retailer, and ilso, known for its pore-care products.

The event will also feature K-pop performances, a Random Dance Challenge, an idol-style makeup show and a dedicated selection of K-pop albums and merchandise.

The pop-up is aimed at introducing emerging Korean beauty brands to consumers and industry professionals in the Czech Republic and across Central and Eastern Europe.

Entry is free, although visitors are encouraged to register online in advance.

The event is organized by Bramasole Prague s.r.o., which operates several Korean restaurant brands in Prague.

World.title: Dancing House Marks 30 Years With a Free Weekend of Dance in Prague
World.content:
Prague’s Dancing House will celebrate its 30th anniversary with a free two-day program of dance classes, performances and workshops on August 29 and 30.

Jiráskovo náměstí, next to the landmark on the Vltava embankment, will host a temporary stage and dance floor throughout the weekend.



The program will run from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. on both Saturday and Sunday.

Visitors can join professional instructors for classes in bachata, street dance and Latin American dance. There will also be sessions for children, dance demonstrations and opportunities to meet and talk with instructors.

The event is open to all levels, with participants able to watch performances or take part in the classes.

Weekend program

The schedule is the same on both days until the evening finale.

11:00 a.m. – Opening

11:05 a.m. – Children’s dance class

11:50 a.m. – Talk with the instructor

12:00 p.m. – Bachata demonstration

12:05 p.m. – Bachata class

12:50 p.m. – Talk with bachata instructors

1:00 p.m. – Street dance demonstration

1:05 p.m. – Street dance class

1:50 p.m. – Talk with the street dance instructor

2:00 p.m. – Latin American dance demonstration

2:05 p.m. – Latin American dance class

2:50 p.m. – Talk with instructors

3:00 p.m. – Hat Jazz performance

3:05 p.m. – Children’s dance class

3:50 p.m. – Talk with the instructor

4:00 p.m. – Bachata demonstration

4:05 p.m. – Bachata class

4:50 p.m. – Talk with bachata instructors

5:00 p.m. – Street dance demonstration

5:05 p.m. – Street dance class

5:50 p.m. – Talk with the street dance instructor

6:00 p.m. – Latin American dance demonstration

6:05 p.m. – Latin American dance class

6:50 p.m. – Talk with instructors

7:00 p.m. – Acrobatic performance

7:05 p.m. – Hula Hoops performance

The closing acrobatic performance will differ each day. Saturday will feature a handstand performance, while Sunday will bring Duo ReAct.

Admission is free. Organizers will also provide light refreshments.

Completed in 1996, the Dancing House is one of Prague’s best-known examples of modern architecture. It stands at the corner of Rašínovo nábřeží and Jiráskovo náměstí, overlooking the Vltava.

The building was designed by Croatian-Czech architect Vlado Milunić in collaboration with Canadian-American architect Frank Gehry. Its curved forms and leaning towers give the impression of a dancing couple, which inspired its Czech name, Tančící dům.

The building is also known by the nickname “Ginger and Fred,” referring to American dancers Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire.

World.title: Bolt Launches App-Free Ride Kiosks in the Czech Republic
World.content:
Bolt has introduced self-service kiosks in the Czech Republic that allow customers to order a ride without a smartphone, mobile data or the Bolt app.

The first kiosk is now operating at Westfield Chodov in Prague. A second will open at Westfield Černý Most on September 1. The company says it plans to consider other high-traffic locations in the future.



The kiosks use TapBox technology and provide access to the same Bolt driver network, pricing and safety standards available through the app.

Customers can place an order directly at the screen, making the service available to people who do not use smartphones or cannot access their phones at the time.

Both shopping centres have also introduced dedicated parking spaces for Bolt drivers collecting passengers. Customers are directed to these designated areas rather than having to meet drivers at potentially unsafe stopping points such as bus stops.

How Bolt kiosks work

Ordering a ride takes several steps. Customers enter their destination, select a ride category and provide their phone number. The available categories are Standard, Comfort, Premium and XL.

Payment is made by card. Once the booking is completed, the kiosk prints a confirmation and sends an SMS containing the vehicle details, estimated arrival time and instructions for finding the driver.

The kiosks operate around the clock and support Czech, English, German, French and Ukrainian.

Each ride booked through a kiosk carries an additional CZK 25 fee.

Bolt says the system could also benefit drivers by connecting them with customers who might otherwise be unable to use the app. The company expects the kiosks to reduce waiting times between rides at busy shopping centres and create additional opportunities for drivers.

The Czech launch follows the introduction of similar kiosks in Slovakia earlier this summer, including at airports.

World.title: Prague Adds 18 Kilometers of Cycle Routes but Cycling Numbers Barely Rise
World.content:
Prague is continuing to expand its cycling infrastructure, but the number of recorded bicycle journeys across the city has remained largely unchanged.

Automatic counters installed on major cycling routes recorded about 5.6 million passages in 2025, roughly 1 percent fewer than the previous year.

After adjusting for counter failures and temporary route closures, however, the Technical Road Administration (TSK) calculated a 0.4 percent increase in cycling traffic.



Prague Adds 18 Kilometers of Routes Away From Traffic

The city added 18 kilometers of two-way cycle paths and other cycling routes separated from motor traffic during the year. The total length of marked cycling routes increased by one kilometer to approximately 550 kilometers.

Routes separated from car traffic now account for 263 kilometers of the network, an increase of seven kilometers compared with the previous year.

TSK operates automatic counters at 31 locations on Prague’s main cycling routes. The devices use induction loops or radar to record cyclists and can determine their direction of travel.

The largest increase in two-way cycling routes came over the past year. Their combined length grew from 63 to 81 kilometers. These routes allow cyclists to travel in both directions on streets that are otherwise one-way for motor vehicles.

New two-way routes were added mainly in Prague 7 around Letná, in Prague 5 in Barrandov, and in Prague 6 around Na Petynce, Rozdělovská and Podbaba.

Modřany Remains Prague’s Busiest Cycling Route

The highest number of cyclists was recorded in Modřany, at the intersection of Vltavanů and U Kino streets. The counter registered 578,016 passages during the year.

Another 540,656 cycling journeys were recorded on Povltavská Street south of Troja Castle.

The largest year-on-year increase was recorded on the Barrandov Bridge, where cycling traffic rose following the completion of its more than two-year reconstruction.

World.title: PM Magyar presses Hungarian businesses to repay Orbán regime spoils
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar urged businesses that benefitted unfairly from contracts awarded under the former Fidesz-KDNP government to repay that money voluntarily in a video message on Facebook on Tuesday.

PM Magyar: “Follow the example of Duna Aszfalt“

“To all of those who, as the anointed of the state, have built up fortunes worth hundreds of billions over the past decade and a half, I have a message: Follow the example of Duna Aszfalt. If public monies went to where they don’t belong, they should be repaid now, voluntarily,” Magyar said.

He warned that later the state would recover those monies anyway, using legal tools. Magyar noted that Duna Aszfalt, a company that won more than HUF 600bn of state contracts in 2018-2020, had decided on Monday to repay early USD 400m of bonds subscribed by the state-owned Magyar Eximbank and Hungarian Development Bank (MFB) to finance a high-risk road project in Africa.

Magyar said the state had reported to authorities more than 20 cases in which public monies exceeding HUF 1,700bn were used inappropriately under the former government. He added that those cases included HUF 640bn of exposure involving a rolling stock order from Egypt and a HUF 360bn state loan for North Macedonia, as well as procurements of alert bracelets for seniors, ambulances, school IT systems and government communications.

Probes and asset recovery

Earlier on Tuesday, he said the foreign ministry had reported a HUF 300bn procurement of ventilators placed during the pandemic under the former head of the portfolio, Péter Szijjártó.

Magyar also highlighted a probe ordered by the government of state contracts with 4iG group as well as efforts to recover assets from public asset management foundations that are not related to higher education. He said that more than HUF 3,000bn had been channeled to the foundations, known by their Hungarian acronym KEKVA, under the Orbán government.

If you missed: Leading candidates for Hungary’s “almighty” National Asset Recovery and Protection Office have presented their programmes

Magyar said the government measures to recover the assets had been taken even as the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) was in the process of being set up.

He said the opposition Fidesz could try to obstruct the establishment of the office, “but to no avail“. “They, too, know, just as do Orbán’s relatives, that whatever was taken illegally from the common wealth of the Hungarian people will be recovered by the Hungarian state,” he added.

Hungarian FM Anita Orbán names new ambassadors: historians tapped for Paris and Warsaw

World.title: Leading candidates for Hungary’s “almighty” National Asset Recovery and Protection Office have presented their programmes
World.content:
Hungary’s new National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH) is tasked with protecting public assets, investigating suspected misuse of state property and helping recover unlawfully acquired public wealth. The relevant legistlation establishing the new body was accepted by the Parliament in July and the body’s head is to be chosen by the National Assembly this Friday. Then the institution’s charter will be accepted in September, so the work can begin.

Hungary’s “almighty” National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) is set to start its work soon, but first the Hungarian Parliament must choose its head. There are three top contestants whose hearing took place today in the Hungarian Parliament’s Justice ad Constitutional Affairs Committee.

Miklós Ligeti: no witch hunt

The accountability not pursued in 1990 must finally be achieved, Miklós Zoltán Ligeti, the legal director of Transparency International Hungary, told the justice and constitutional affairs committee of parliament on Tuesday during his hearing as a nominee for the head of the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH). He added that while asset recovery and accountability must begin, the office itself must be established first.

Miklós Ligeti, one of the candidates for the post of the head of Hungary’s new National Asset Recovery and Protection Office. Photo: MTI

NVVVH’s mandate will not be limited to the past 16 years. “It is not a NER-purging office,” he said, referring to the moniker “system of national cooperation” of the Orbán regime. A legal procedure cannot be turned into a witch hunt, he added. Ligeti emphasised that the new authority must cooperate with many other bodies in the fight against corruption. Without this, the entire process is doomed to fail, he said.

In response to a question, Ligeti stressed that the primary goal is to restore public trust in the state. On the risk of political retribution, he said he did not see why this office should be feared more than any other authority.

Anna Róza Unger: developing an immune system

The first six-year mandate of the leader of the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) will suffice to uncover “what happened in this country“, but the cases are not expected to end in binding sentences within that period, political scientist Anna Róza Unger said before parliament’s judicial and constitutional affairs committee on Tuesday.

Unger, who is vying for the position of head of the NVVH, said the mandate will be enough to launch the procedures “to bring everyone responsible, be it a big man or a small one, a city mouse or a country one, before the court.” This would go for “all who committed it, those who allowed [crimes] to be committed, and for Hungarian society to grasp and learn what had happened so it can never happen again,” she said.

The NVVH will work to map the system that created and operated corruption rather than to unveil concrete cases, she said, “so that the newly forming Hungarian democracy may develop an immune system which, after a period of consolidation, makes re-occurrence impossible,” Unger said.

Nicholas Sárvári: NVVH ‘must become rule of law’

Hungary’s Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) “should become an integral part of the rule of law“, Nicholas Sárvári, the Tisza Party’s nominee to head the new organisation, said in parliament’s judicial committee on Tuesday.

Péter Magyar’s government granted unprecedented powers for the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office. Photo: Facebook/TISZA Párt

Sárvári noted that the structure of the authority was defined by law, and said that as its head he would “find the right experts for each task“. The candidate suggested that the way public assets had been handled in Hungary in previous years was “unacceptable“, adding that he felt “ashamed as a Hungarian“. Restoring public trust and building transparency will be one of the main tasks of the new authority, he added.

Photo: MTI

If you missed – The Guardian: Hungary is ‘de-Orbánising’ at record speed

Former PM Orbán’s party does not take part in the procedure

The Hungarian Parliament is expected to elect NVVH’s leader on Friday and adopt its charter during the autumn session, with the authority expected to be set up later in the season.

Péter Magyar’s Tisza has supermajority in the Hungarian Parliamet, so it will depend only on their MPs who the head of the new body will be. Photo: Facebook/Forsthoffer Ágnes

The Hungarian Civil Liberties Union (TASZ), the Hungarian Helsinki Committee, the K-Monitor Public Benefit Association and the World Federation of Hungarians were represented at the meeting in a consultative capacity.

Former government party and main opposition party Fidesz and its ally, KDNP did not send their MPs to the hearing.

World.title: Hungary’s overpriced Covid ventilator mystery: Why thousands are still gathering dust in warehouses
World.content:
Anita Orbán, the foreign minister, has filed a criminal complaint concerning purchases related to ventilators purchased during the coronavirus pandemic under the previous Orbán government.

Brutal amount of money spent

The complaint concerns purchases made in March and April 2020, worth a total 300 billion forints (EUR 827m) by the previous foreign ministry led by Péter Szijjártó, Orbán said, adding that the purchases had been made outside the public procurement system.

The documents reviewed so far have raised “suspicion of embezzlement causing extreme damage and other crimes … suggesting the responsibility of top management” at the previous ministry, Orbán said, adding that the procurement had mostly targeted ventilators.

Former FM Szijjártó looking at a ventilator. Photo: Facebook/Szijjártó Péter

The ministry has established that its predecessor had “overpurchased“, buying too many equipment, while there was “a significant difference between purchase and producer prices”, she said.

Lack of staff was the bottleneck, not the number of vetilators

The minister noted that an invasive ventilator requires an ICU specialist, a qualified nurse, oxygen supply, and an ICU bed, which at the time of the pandemic limited the number of patients in intensive care to between 800-2,000. “The bottleneck was not the restricted number of ventilators … despite that fact, the decision makers considered the number of ventilators as an indicator of the full capacity,” she said, adding that “at the height of the epidemic only 2,500 ventilators had been sent to the hospitals, the vast majority of the stock is still in a warehouse.“

As for the purchase price of the equipment, the difference from the producer price was 13.4 billion forints in the case of six companies, she said. Quoting press reports, she said the average price of a ventilator was 17 million forints, while producers sold the same models between 1,000 and 5,000 US dollars (348,000-1.3m forints).

If you missed: The Hungarian government bought Chinese ventilators known to be dangerous

Szijjártó tried to hide important details

According to the minister, the previous ministry had left behind “incomplete documentation” but added that the original documents “could not be fully erased and a lot of them could be restored, which provided a better image of what happened.” She added that her ministry’s staff had managed to restore 130,000 files concerning the procurement.

According to information from the ministry, its predecessor had purchased 16,853 ventilators, protective gear, PCR tests, and medicines in spring 2020, under the previous government’s “special legal order” introduced at the beginning of the pandemic.

World.title: Previously unseen footage of Hungarian Gripen crash as minister reveals how disaster unfolded – updated: surgery
World.content:
One of the Hungarian Defence Forces’ Gripen fighter jets crashed on the grounds of Szolnok military airfield on Monday after suffering a malfunction during a training mission. The pilot ejected from the aircraft. Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, the Defence Minister and former Chief of the General Staff, has revealed fresh details of the incident, which could have resulted in an even more serious catastrophe and endangered further lives at the military airfield. He said the outcome depended on the experience and presence of mind of the 51-year-old pilot.

Gripens were practising high-speed interceptions

As we reported on Monday, the aircraft had been conducting high-speed interception drills in Hungarian airspace alongside another Gripen. After completing a second exercise, however, a fault warning appeared and the mission was abandoned. The two aircraft then headed for Szolnok, as the malfunctioning fighter could no longer safely return to its home base at Kecskemét.

Drones were used to search the burning wreck after the crash to determine whether firefighters were safe to start their work or not, considering the large amount of explosives the Gripen fighter jet was carrying during the exercise. Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

The pilot ejected during the landing, while firefighters arriving at the scene extinguished the blaze within minutes.

The aircraft was carrying air-to-air missiles and ammunition for its cannon, meaning the consequences could have been considerably worse had the pilot made an error. The cause of the crash remains under investigation, but Ruszin-Szendi gave important new details in an interview with Gábor Bochkor on Retro Radio’s morning programme.

‘All instruments went black’

Ruszin-Szendi said the Gripen was being flown by a 51-year-old pilot with more than 2,000 flying hours, including experience on international operations. The fighter pilot was in excellent physical condition but suffered spinal injuries in the crash and was undergoing surgery at the Honvéd Hospital.

The last Gripen accident took place in 2015 in Hungary. Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

According to the minister, the two aircraft had taken off from Kecskemét to practise high-speed interceptions. They successfully completed the first exercise and returned, but warnings began appearing in rapid succession at the end of the second interception. The cockpit instruments then went black.

Ruszin-Szendi said this made for an especially difficult situation because Gripens have no analogue instruments. In such circumstances, the pilot cannot read the aircraft’s speed or altitude from conventional dials, but must instead fly primarily by visual reference.

Aircraft began veering to the right

The situation was eased somewhat by the fact that radio contact between the two Gripens was not lost. With assistance from the accompanying aircraft, the malfunctioning fighter reached Szolnok airfield, where the pilot managed to land.

Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

The difficulties did not end there, however. The aircraft began veering to the right on the runway, and the pilot ejected only after realising that he could no longer regain control.

Ruszin-Szendi said the pilot had attempted until the final moment to save the fighter jet, estimated to be worth around 30 billion forints, while also putting his own life at risk.

The pilot risked his life to save the jet. Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

He added that ejection was no easy ordeal, as it could itself impose severe physical strain. A pilot may be subjected to forces of up to 15 to 20 G — 15 to 20 times the force of gravity — which is believed to have occurred in this case and may have contributed to the spinal injury.

If you missed – Polish bus driver speaks out after deadly Hungary crash: ‘No words can ease the families’ pain’

The injury may also have been worsened by the pilot landing on the concrete after ejecting.

Ruszin-Szendi visited the injured pilot in hospital. The airman was said to have been pleased that he could move all his limbs, and had already asked when he could return to flying duties.

Saab seeks answers over crash

The question now is how Hungary will replace the lost Gripen. Ruszin-Szendi said a decision could be made only once the investigation had established what happened.

Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

Swedish manufacturer Saab is also keen to determine the precise cause of the accident and is providing technical assistance to the inquiry. The minister said relations with the manufacturer were good, though negotiations over the price of a possible replacement aircraft would be a separate matter.

The minister made it clear that the Hungarian Defence Forces have the ability to protect NATO airspace despite the accident. He added that the Hungarian pilots were keen to fly again on the Gripen jets despite the ongoing investigation and the possible dangers. Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

The flight recorders have yet to be analysed, and there is still no definitive explanation for the crash.

Update: Gripen pilot expected to fully recover after operation

A successful operation has been performed on the pilot of the Gripen aircraft that crashed on Monday, the defence minister said on Facebook after receiving information from the hospital. Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said the pilot was expected to make a full recovery. Ruszin-Szendi said he hoped the pilot could fly again soon. “It is his greatest wish and we cannot wish him otherwise,” the minister said. The jet, belonging to the Hungarian military, crashed near Szolnok, in eastern Hungary. The pilot could eject from the aircraft but was hospitalised with a spinal injury.

World.title: How Hungary’s central bank squandered EUR 30.4 million in two years — inquiry concerning luxury project begins
World.content:
Built for almost EUR 55 million, closed after two years and now on sale for EUR 25 million: the Hungarian central bank’s luxury development on Lake Balaton. Those responsible for a development in Balatonakarattya, on which the Hungarian National Bank’s foundation spent almost EUR 55 million, may soon be identified, Ágnes Forsthoffer, Speaker of Parliament, said.

Lake Balaton ‘brought into’ luxury complex

The Tisza Party politician said that the central bank’s foundation had built an education and conference centre on the site of a former MÁV children’s holiday camp, describing it as a “sinkhole for public money”. Forsthoffer said that the project was a particularly striking example of how taxpayers’ money had previously been handled, MTI wrote.

She also noted that the luxury complex had operated for barely two years. The facility was available exclusively to MNB employees as a holiday venue before being closed on cost-cutting grounds. The property was subsequently put up for sale for EUR 25 million.

Forsthoffer highlighted another unusual feature of the scheme: she claimed that Lake Balaton itself had effectively been “brought into” the estate’s grounds, atv.hu wrote. The politician branded the arrangement “utterly outrageous”.

Inquiry into central bank project to begin

A parliamentary committee of inquiry into alleged abuses connected with the operation of the Hungarian National Bank is due to begin work on Wednesday. Forsthoffer said that its investigation could soon establish who was responsible for the Balatonakarattya project — and who benefited from Hungarian taxpayers’ money.

Parliament committee to start investigation in the issue soon. Photo: Facebook/TISZA Párt

World.title: Hungary to reclaim EUR 303 million as government moves to scrap controversial foundations
World.content:
The ministry of science and technology will recover a total HUF 110 billion (EUR 303 million) through the elimination of public interest asset management foundations (KEKVA), Zoltán Tanács, the minister, said on Facebook on Monday.

Tanács said his portfolio would take over the activities of the ZalaZONE and Élvonal foundations, adding that while the “redundant” foundations would be scrapped, the ministry would maintain their activities. He also added that scrapping the system would save the ministry an annual HUF 800 million.

According to Tanács, the two foundations have a combined HUF 62.5 billion on their accounts, while they also have assets worth nearly HUF 50 billion. “That is over HUF 110 billion – from now on in public funds,” the minister added.

Tanács said both Élvonal’s and ZalaZONE’s activities were crucial, the first focusing on the development of young talents and building world-class scientific teams and the latter having an automotive research and development infrastructure, which could provide a test environment for self-driving cars, drones and robots in future. “But all that does not require an unnecessarily expensive, not sufficiently transparent or controlled foundation model,” he added.

World.title: Hungarian FM Anita Orbán names new ambassadors: historians tapped for Paris and Warsaw
World.content:
Prominent historians and specialists are among the latest nominees for key ambassadorial and consular posts. Hungary’s Foreign Minister Anita Orbán has announced several new nominees for ambassadorial and consular positions, including historians selected for key posts in Paris and Warsaw.

Speaking on ATV’s Egyenes Beszéd on Monday evening, Orbán said the government had so far replaced 34 of Hungary’s 138 heads of mission since the change of government. She stressed that most of the new appointments were career diplomats, although several well-known experts from academia and other fields have also been selected.

Among the latest nominees are historian Balázs Ablonczy for Paris, election expert Mátyás Bódi for Barcelona, historian and Poland specialist Miklós Mitrovits for Warsaw, and China expert Tamás Hajba for Beijing.

Historian nominated for Paris

Ablonczy, a historian specialising in Hungarian-French relations, has been asked to serve as Hungary’s ambassador in Paris. He previously headed the Hungarian Institute in Paris between 2011 and 2015. Orbán described him as one of the country’s leading experts on Hungarian-French diplomatic relations, making his nomination one of the most notable among the latest appointments.

The Warsaw nomination has also gone to a historian. Mitrovits, a prominent Polish studies expert, currently teaches at a Polish university and has extensive experience researching Poland and Hungarian-Polish relations.

Election expert to become Barcelona consul general

One of the more unexpected names on the list is Mátyás Bódi, who became widely known in Hungary through his work on electoral geography. Orbán has asked Bódi to become Hungary’s consul general in Barcelona, although the nominees are currently at different stages of the appointment process.

The foreign minister said the government was seeking to select people with relevant professional expertise, language skills and knowledge of the countries and regions where they will serve. “These names also illustrate that we are trying to find the best person for every location,” Orbán said, highlighting professional preparedness and integrity alongside knowledge of the relevant language and bilateral relationship.

China post goes to an experienced China specialist

Tamás Hajba has been selected as Hungary’s next ambassador to Beijing. Unlike some of the other newly announced names, Hajba has a long career in diplomacy and international economic policy. He spent more than a decade working at Hungary’s Foreign Ministry before joining the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) in Paris, where he worked as a China specialist.

Orbán said the majority of the newly selected heads of mission were career diplomats, with Hajba among those appointments. She also said the government was trying to match diplomats to posts where their existing knowledge and experience could be put to the best use.

Why has Hungary recalled 34 ambassadors?

Orbán also addressed the government’s decision to recall 34 heads of mission since taking office. She rejected the idea that all of those diplomats had been recalled simply because they were associated with the previous Fidesz government. According to the minister, some were replaced because they had already spent an unusually long period in their posts.

Under previous governments, some ambassadors remained abroad for as long as 10 or even 12 years. Orbán argued that lengthy postings can create a diplomatic problem, as questions may eventually arise over whether a diplomat has become too closely embedded in the interests of the country where they serve.

The new government plans to restore a more traditional rotation system. Under the proposed arrangement, ambassadors and consuls general would spend four years on a foreign posting before returning to Hungary for at least one year.

World.title: Hungarian Gripen crash: Swedish Saab offers support as investigation begins
World.content:
The fighter jet that crashed near Szolnok on Monday was a single-seat Gripen C, not the latest E/F model. Saab says it will assist the Hungarian investigation, while the crash has also briefly affected the Swedish defence company’s share price.

Saab has confirmed that the Hungarian Gripen fighter jet that crashed near Szolnok on Monday was a single-seat Gripen C. The Hungarian pilot ejected from the aircraft and survived the crash. Hungarian authorities are responsible for investigating what caused the accident, while Saab says it will provide technical assistance to the investigation.

“Of course, Saab will assist in the investigation,” Mattias Rådström, the company’s press manager, told Swedish news agency Direkt.

Gripen developed a fault during a training flight

The aircraft was flying alongside another Gripen during a training exercise when a warning indicating a malfunction appeared in the cockpit. The training mission was aborted, and the two aircraft headed towards Szolnok, as the damaged fighter could reportedly no longer reach Kecskemét.

However, another incident occurred during the final stage of the landing. The pilot decided to eject, after which the aircraft left the runway area and caught fire.

The pilot survived the ejection and is currently reported to be in a stable condition.

Hungary’s air force has suspended Gripen training flights until the investigation is completed. The aircraft assigned to alert and operational duties continue to perform their missions. Investigators have already begun examining the crash site, while data from the fighter’s flight recorder – commonly known as its black box – could prove crucial in determining exactly what happened.

Could Hungary ground its Gripen fleet?

Saab has not announced a general flight ban for the Gripen following the accident. Asked whether the aircraft could potentially be grounded while the investigation is under way, Rådström said the company would have to return to the question if such a decision became necessary.

The crash leaves Hungary with 17 Gripen aircraft in service.

Saab said in June that it had completed deliveries under an additional agreement signed by Sweden’s Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) and Hungary’s Ministry of Defence in January 2024. Hungary had subsequently operated a total of 18 Gripen C/D aircraft: 16 single-seat Gripen C fighters and two two-seat Gripen D aircraft. Hungary has not purchased the newer Gripen E/F variant.

The Gripen is a single-engine, supersonic multirole fighter designed for missions including air combat, ground attack and reconnaissance.

The shares subsequently recovered much of the lost ground. By around noon, Saab stock was up approximately 0.1% for the day.

World.title: Bucharest International Poetry Festival to take place in September
World.content:
The Bucharest International Poetry Festival (FIPB) is set to bring together poets and artists from around the world between September 14 and 20.

Organized by the Bucharest City Hall through the National Museum of Romanian Literature, this year’s festival proposes the theme “Slow Gun Poetry/Long-Range Poetry,” inspired by poet Cezar Ivănescu’s reflection on the power of a simple sign on a sheet of paper.

According to the organizers, the theme starts from the idea that from a word, ideas, consciences and even revolutions can be born, and that the true strength of the world does not lie in force, but in meaning.

“Poetry is not a form of escape from reality, but one of the most powerful ways of understanding it. At a time when words are increasingly used to separate, radicalize and build walls between people, the Bucharest International Poetry Festival assumes, through this edition, the mission of bringing the word back to its natural space: that of dialogue, freedom, empathy and the meeting between people and cultures,” said Ioan Cristescu, general director of the National Museum of Romanian Literature, cited in the press release.

This year’s edition features guests from the Republic of Armenia, Austria, the Czech Republic, Cyprus, China, Croatia, France, Greece, Italy, Lithuania, the Republic of Moldova, Peru, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Tunisia and Turkey, alongside numerous Romanian poets and artists. More than 50 events are included in the festival program: public readings, debates, conferences, exhibitions, concerts, performances, recitals and commemorative events.

The festival will officially open on Monday, September 14, at 18:00, in the Hall of the “Carol I” Central University Library. The opening ceremony will bring together representatives of partner cultural and diplomatic institutions, as well as ambassadors and representatives of cultural institutes from participating countries.

The evening will continue with a concert performed by the ARCO Chamber Ensemble, public readings by Romanian and international poets, and a reading-performance by Slovenian poet Aleš Šteger, recognized as one of the most original and translated voices in contemporary European literature, accompanied on accordion by Tori Jure.

An important component of this year’s edition of FIPB is dedicated to the memory and recovery of great Romanian poets. The program includes commemorative events dedicated to Cezar Ivănescu, Emil Botta, Constanța Buzea, Angela Marinescu, Marin Sorescu and Magda Isanos, organized in partnership with the Bucharest National Theatre. At the same time, this year’s edition marks 130 years since the birth of Tristan Tzara, founder of the Dada movement, through a workshop dedicated to children and adults, in which poetry meets visual art and calligrams.

Moreover, FIPB will feature programs dedicated to children and teenagers, such as comic book workshops, creative activities, literary games and numerous other projects.

World.title: Romania’s football team to face off against Sweden in Nations League match next month
World.content:
Romania’s national football team is set to play against Sweden on Friday, September 25, within League B of the Nations League. The match will be played in Solna, Sweden, according to an announcement on the official FRF website.

Starting Tuesday, August 25, and until Friday, September 18 (or until they run out), tickets for the game against Sweden will be available on the FRF website. The price of a ticket, set by the organizers of the match, is RON 130, with 2,200 seats in the stadium’s North Stand (sectors 116-121) allocated to the Romanian fans. Each supporter can order a maximum of 4 tickets before completing an order, and the tickets will be nominative.

Group B4 of the Nations League also includes Bosnia-Herzegovina and Poland. After the match with Sweden, the Romanian team will face Bosnia-Herzegovina on September 28, then Poland on October 2.

Rematches will take place on October 5 against Sweden, November 14 against Poland, and November 17 against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

The winner of the group will be promoted to League A of the Nations League, while the team finishing second will play a promotion play-off.

Romania managed to gain promotion to League B in the last edition of the Nations League, after winning the group with six wins in the same number of matches. This performance allowed the national team to reach the play-offs for the 2026 World Cup, although they finished third in their group in the qualifiers.

World.title: Bucharest included in ranking of cities with highest potential for AI data center development
World.content:
Romania’s capital ranks 21st in the Savills Power and Place Index, the global ranking that assesses cities with the strongest potential for future data center development based on criteria such as energy availability, telecommunications infrastructure, access to resources and project delivery capability.

According to Savills’s report, the next wave of investment in digital infrastructure will increasingly target markets capable of supporting the accelerated expansion of artificial intelligence. The same report showed that global investment in data centers has reached record levels, fueled by the expansion of major hyperscale operators and growing demand driven by artificial intelligence. In this context, the challenge is no longer the availability of capital, but rather identifying locations capable of providing the power, land and infrastructure required for large-scale developments.

Savills highlighted that many established European hubs are already experiencing limitations related to power grid capacity, land availability and permitting processes, creating opportunities for emerging cities and markets with greater resource availability.

According to real estate consultant Crosspoint Real Estate, Romania benefits from several structural advantages relevant to digital infrastructure development. These include a high level of fiber-optic coverage, competitive internet speeds and affordable data service costs, all of which support large-scale data transfer and processing.

At the same time, data consumption continues to grow rapidly both in Romania and across the Central and Eastern European region, driven by the expansion of cloud services, the digitalization of the economy and the integration of artificial intelligence solutions into business operations. This trend is increasing the need for local and regional digital infrastructure and is supporting the development of data centers located closer to end users.

At present, however, one significant disadvantage is the cost of electricity. Nevertheless, with the commissioning of the Iernut and Mintia power plants, as well as the projected development of energy storage facilities in the medium term, Romania could become increasingly attractive for this segment.

“While traditional European hubs are facing increasing constraints related to energy access, land availability and development restrictions, Bucharest is emerging as a well-positioned market for the next wave of investments in digital infrastructure supporting AI development. For data center investors, access to power and connectivity is becoming just as important as location,” said Emilian Podaru, MRICS, Head of Industrial & Logistics at Crosspoint Real Estate, the International Associate of Savills in Romania.

The report estimated that data center expansion will also have a significant impact on the industrial and logistics sector. Across Europe, the growth of this ecosystem could generate additional demand for approximately 790,000 sq m of logistics space over the next three years, required for storage, equipment, operations, and related services.

World.title: “Seaside for Everyone” program aims to attract tourists to Romanian seaside in September
World.content:
The 49th edition of “Seaside for Everyone,” a well-known program that aims to attract tourists to the Romanian seaside through massive price cuts in accommodation, was announced on Tuesday, August 25, by the Federation of Associations of Romanian Tourism Employers (FPTR).

Initiated and coordinated by FPTR and supported through the participation of economic operators on the seaside, “Seaside for Everyone” advances holidays on the seaside at reduced rates for tourists.

The program takes place from September 1-30, 2026.

To date, 67 accommodation units from 10 resorts and tourist areas are enrolled. According to FPTR, a novelty of this year’s edition is the change in the list of participants. 24 of the units currently enrolled did not participate in the spring edition. Among them are units entering the program for the first time, as well as returning operators.

Moreover, compared with the spring edition, when the lowest rate communicated was RON 42/person/night, the current edition starts at RON 39/person/night for accommodation without meals, in Eforie Nord.

The minimum rates communicated by other participating units are RON 39 (EUR 7.43) in Eforie Nord, RON 65 (EUR 12.38) in Eforie Sud, RON 60 (EUR 11.43) in Costinești, RON 58 (EUR 11.05) in Neptun-Olimp, RON 74 (EUR 14.10) in Jupiter, RON 77 (EUR 14.67) in Saturn, RON 108 (EUR 20.57) in Mangalia, RON 80 (EUR 15.24) in Vama Veche, RON 69 (EUR 13.14) in Mamaia, and RON 65 (EUR 12.38) in Mamaia Nord.

The rates, the included services, and participation periods are established by each accommodation unit. Some offers are for accommodation, while others include breakfast or All Inclusive services. The packages can also be paid for with holiday vouchers, under the conditions accepted by each accommodation unit or travel agency.

Although the official period of the program is September 1–30, 2026, some units have submitted offers that continue into October. As such, tourists have more holiday options in the off-season, while operators can maintain their activity for a longer period.

The list of participating units, rates, validity periods and contact details is published on the official website of the Federation of Associations of Romanian Tourism Employers. The list is updated as FPTR receives new registrations.

World.title: Romanian MP Claudiu Năsui accepts nomination as Moldova’s economy minister
World.content:
Romanian lawmaker Claudiu Năsui accepted prime minister Vasile Tofan’s invitation to join the Moldovan government as minister of economic development and digitalization. The Save Romania Union (USR) deputy said the move would require him to resign from Romania’s Parliament.

“I have accepted the position of economy minister in the government of the Republic of Moldova,” Năsui announced on Facebook. He said he strongly agreed with Tofan’s vision of turning Moldova into “the most welcoming country for entrepreneurs.”

Claudiu Năsui said he would use his experience to support economic reforms, including the liberalization and privatization process started after the fall of communism. He also linked Moldova’s economic development to its efforts to join the European Union and strengthen ties with Romania.

“I chose to accept Mr. Tofan’s invitation to join the government of the Republic of Moldova, even though this step means giving up my mandate as a member of the Romanian Parliament and dedicating my experience to a new reform effort,” Năsui said.

“A more prosperous Moldovan economy also means a more prosperous Romanian economy as part of our shared European path,” he added.

Vasile Tofan announced that Claudiu Năsui would be proposed for the position of minister of economic development and digitalization, citing his economic education, private-sector experience, and previous involvement in government reforms.

Năsui studied economics at Paris Dauphine University and finance at Bocconi University. He has worked in the financial sector, including at PwC and Romanian bank BCR, and holds the Chartered Financial Analyst certification.

He was first elected to the Romanian Parliament in 2016 and served as Romania’s economy minister between 2020 and 2021. He also founded the Open Budget platform, which tracks public spending.

According to prime minister Tofan, Claudiu Năsui’s priorities in Moldova will include reducing bureaucracy, addressing problems at state-owned companies, cutting public expenditure, and removing obstacles faced by small and medium-sized enterprises.

“We need this type of energy at the Economy Ministry,” Vasile Tofan said. “We want the Economy Ministry to become one of the main drivers of state reform and economic growth.”

The Moldovan prime minister also announced that Eugeniu Osmochescu would be proposed as minister of agriculture and food industry. His responsibilities will include preparing Moldovan agriculture for EU accession and improving the sector’s competitiveness and resilience to climate change.

World.title: Romanian Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes winner Fjord draws over 150,000 viewers after French release
World.content:
Fjord, the latest film from Romanian director Cristian Mungiu, attracted more than 150,000 viewers shortly after opening in France on August 19. France is the first of more than 100 territories where the Palme d’Or-winning film is due to receive a theatrical release.

The film ranked first in box-office receipts during both its previews and its official opening day, when it was seen by 30,058 people, including 11,727 in Paris, according to a press release. By the end of its first weekend, it had drawn 140,346 viewers in cinemas, with the Paris audience accounting for 51,847 admissions.

Including preview screenings, Fjord reached a total audience of 151,121 across 270 cinemas. Its distribution is expanding to 290 screens this week.

“Based on the ratio between its first-day box-office revenue and final audience figures, Fjord could attract more than 800,000 viewers in France,” reads the announcement.

The film is distributed in France by Le Pacte, which has handled all of Cristian Mungiu’s films since 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days. The latter, which won the filmmaker his first Palme d’Or in 2007, attracted around 380,000 viewers in France.

The release figures place Fjord ahead of the opening-day performance of some other recent Palme d’Or winners. Jafar Panahi’s It Was Just an Accident, the 2025 winner, debuted with 20,000 viewers and eventually reached 700,000 admissions, while Sean Baker’s Anora opened at a level close to Fjord and finished with 654,000 viewers.

Cristian Mungiu’s film won the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival in May, along with the FIPRESCI Prize, the Citizenship Prize, the François Chalais Prize, and the Ecumenical Jury Prize.

Fjord was also shown to 43,440 viewers in Romania during a one-off screening on June 13. Distribution also began in French-speaking Switzerland in August, with releases scheduled for September in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Greece, Italy, and Belgium.

Fjord tells the story of Lisbet and Mihai Gheorghiu, a married couple who move to a small village on a Norwegian fjord. They soon befriend their neighbors, the Halberg family, while the children of the two households grow close despite differences in upbringing and values. The cast includes Sebastian Stan, Renate Reinsve, Adrian Titieni, Alin Panc, Giulia Nahmany, and Ana Bodea.
