World.title: Azerbaijan amends structure of Primorsky Boulevard Administration
Uzbekistan, South Korea deepen business ties at Tashkent Forum
World.content:
Photo: the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade of Uzbekistany of

BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 25. Uzbekistan intends to expand its trade and investment ties with South Korea, with a particular focus on ways to increase exports to the South Korean market and launch new joint projects.

This was reflected in the statement by the Uzbek Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, following the Uzbekistan–Korea Business Forum and B2B meetings held in Tashkent on August 24.

According to the information, the meeting was organized by the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade (MIIT) in cooperation with the Korea Importers Association (KOIMA).

The Ministry notes that the event brought together Deputy Minister Ilzat Kasimov, KOIMA Chairperson Yun Young-mi, South Korean Ambassador to Uzbekistan Won Do Yeon, and about 100 business representatives from both countries.

Meanwhile, bilateral trade between Uzbekistan and South Korea reached nearly $2 billion in 2025, while cumulative Korean investment in Uzbekistan exceeded $8 billion. More than 600 companies with Korean capital currently operate in Uzbekistan.

The forum focused on expanding bilateral trade, increasing exports of Uzbek products to South Korea, developing new business partnerships and advancing joint investment projects.

Particular attention was given to cooperation in agriculture, industry, energy, logistics and telecommunications, as the two sides explored opportunities to deepen private-sector ties and create new commercial channels.

The B2B meetings provided Uzbek and Korean companies with an opportunity to discuss specific export and investment opportunities, including potential partnerships and joint projects.

The growing business engagement comes as Uzbekistan seeks to expand access to foreign markets and attract investment into higher-value industries, while South Korean companies are strengthening their presence in Uzbekistan’s industrial and technology sectors.

The forum is expected to support further direct contacts between businesses and help translate bilateral economic ties into concrete trade and investment projects.

World.title: Azerbaijan simplifies visa procedures for foreigners arriving for Formula 1
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 25. President Ilham Aliyev has signed an order simplifying visa procedures for foreigners and stateless persons traveling to Azerbaijan for the Formula 1 race to be held in Baku in 2026.

The information was published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan.

Under the order, foreigners and stateless persons arriving in Azerbaijan in connection with the 2026 Formula 1 race who present any of the documents listed below will be eligible to obtain visas at Azerbaijan’s international airports from August 25 through September 30, 2026.

Any one of the following documents will serve as a basis for visa issuance:

An accreditation card or other document confirming accreditation in accordance with the relevant rules of Formula One Management Limited, the international organizer of Formula 1 races, and the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA);

An accreditation card confirming accreditation with the Baku City Circuit Operations Company;

A ticket to the 2026 Formula 1 race in Baku, including an electronic ticket, or a document confirming the purchase of a ticket.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Azerbaijan is tasked with informing Formula One Management Limited, the FIA, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) and relevant authorities of foreign countries about the simplified visa procedures for foreigners and stateless persons arriving in Azerbaijan in connection with the 2026 Formula 1 race in Baku.

The ministry is also tasked with ensuring that information on the simplified visa procedures, as well as the possibility for foreigners and stateless persons to obtain electronic visas through the ASAN Visa system, is published on the ministry’s websites and the websites of Azerbaijani embassies and consulates abroad.

The State Migration Service of Azerbaijan is tasked with informing airlines operating flights to Azerbaijan about the simplified visa procedures for foreigners and stateless persons arriving in the country in connection with the 2026 Formula 1 race in Baku.

World.title: Kazakhstan Railways boosts coal shipments ahead of heating season
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 25. Kazakhstan's national railway company Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) transported more than 19.5 million tons of coal from May through August 2026 in preparation for the new heating season, KTZ's press service reported.

Of the total volume, 18.3 million tons were delivered to thermal power plants, while 1.2 million tons were transported for household needs. The volumes are in line with the same period of the previous heating season.

Coal transportation has been fully secured with rolling stock. KTZ's subsidiary Kaztemirtrans operates 29,000 gondola cars, including 18,500 used for coal transportation each month. During peak periods, up to 3,000 additional gondola cars can be deployed.

KTZ said there is currently no shortage of rolling stock.

The railway infrastructure is also being prepared for higher transportation volumes. In 2026, track repairs are being carried out along 1,577 kilometers, including 573 kilometers of major repairs.

Several projects aimed at increasing the capacity of coal transportation routes are also nearing completion, including modernization of the Aksu-1 - Degelen, Kyzylzhar - Zhezkazgan and Tobol - Kandyagash sections, as well as the extension of receiving and departure tracks on the Moyynty - Zharik section.

The Karaganda-Sortirovochnaya station's classification yard is also being modernized to increase its processing capacity.

"The main pressure on coal transportation is expected in September-November, when around 3 million tons of coal, or 45% of the annual household demand, are to be delivered. The peak is expected in October, with transportation volumes reaching 1.1 million tons, equivalent to around 520 railcars per day - twice the current loading level", the company said.

KTZ called on local authorities and regional operators to ensure that coal is transported to consumers as much as possible before the peak period.

World.title: Lockerbie bombing trial delayed after new evidence discovered
World.content:
A US judge has postponed the trial of the man authorities allege built the bomb that blew New York-bound Pan Am flight 103 out of the sky over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing 270 people in 1988.

Jury selection had been scheduled to begin on Wednesday, local time, in the trial of Abu Agila Mohammad Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi, a Libyan intelligence operative who prosecutors allege once confessed to his role in the 1988 bombing.

In the decision to postpone the trial, US District Judge Dabney Friedrich cited the discovery of new evidence that defence attorneys want to examine.

The judge said "the newly discovered evidence, as well as evidence located in other countries" and "the need for the defence to determine how best to defend this case" made her reach the decision.

Abu Agila Mohammad Masud Kheir Al-Marimi is accused of making the bomb that blew up Pan Am flight 103 over Lockerbie. (Reuters/Alexandria, VA Sheriff's Office)

Judge Friedrich did not schedule a new trial date but set a court hearing on September 1 to discuss next steps.

Mr Mas'ud, now in his mid-70s, has pleaded not guilty to two criminal charges related to the destruction of the aircraft resulting in death and faces a maximum of life in prison if convicted.

The Boeing 747 exploded minutes after take-off from London on December 21, 1988, killing all 259 people on board, including 190 Americans, and 11 people on the ground in Scotland.

Loading...

The bombing made former Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, whose government accepted responsibility for the attack in 2003, an international pariah.

Mr Mas'ud has denied wrongdoing and his lawyers have challenged the credibility of evidence gathered by prosecutors, including Mr Mas'ud's alleged confession to a Libyan police officer in 2012, a year after rebel forces toppled Gaddafi's government.

Mr Mas'ud's trial in Washington DC federal court has been delayed by years of legal wrangling over the alleged confession and other issues that have exposed the complexities of a US prosecution over a decades-old attack in Britain with crucial evidence gathered in Libya.

Mr Mas'ud, who was arrested in Libya and brought to the US in 2022, is accused of building a time-delayed bomb that was packed into a suitcase and placed in checked baggage in Malta.

The explosive-laden suitcase eventually made its way to London Heathrow Airport, where it was stored in the hold of Pan Am flight 103.

Reuters

World.title: Israeli Knesset member vandalises Palestinian memorial in West Bank
World.content:
A right wing Israeli politician has recorded himself taking a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in the occupied West Bank, after being escorted into the village by Israeli soldiers.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) accused Zvi Sukkot of having "acted deceptively and manipulatively" in requesting its protection at the site, confirming it diverted resources to accompany Mr Sukkot only for him to carry out the vandalism.

The 35-year-old member of the Knesset posted video of his attempt to destroy the stone memorial in the town of Madama, south of the city of Nablus, arguing it was a "terror monument".

"Every child who sees a giant monument every day that glorifies Jewish murderers, dreams of being a terrorist," he said on social media.

"There is no place for support for terror in the State of Israel!"

Loading...

Israel's occupation of the West Bank has been deemed unlawful by the International Court of Justice, in an advisory opinion published in 2024.

Video of the incident from witnesses to the vandalism had already spread on social media by the time Mr Sukkot posted his own.

Those videos show soldiers watching on as Israeli settlers hit the monument, which memorialises Palestinians killed over decades, with a military vehicle parked nearby.

In a statement, the IDF said it had received an application for protection from Mr Sukkot earlier in August ahead of a tour of three West Bank villages.

"Contrary to the agreed-upon coordination, the participants acted deceptively and manipulatively, without authorisation, departing entirely from the approved framework, and began demolishing one of the monuments in Madama," it said.

"Upon identifying what was taking place, the soldiers reported the incident to their commanders, who instructed them to stop the activity, and the participants were quickly escorted out of the village.

"IDF soldiers assigned to operational missions in the area were diverted to this task and placed at unnecessary risk while the IDF is operating under significant operational strain."

IDF criticises 'misuse' of resources, but not destruction of memorial

The damaged monument in the West Bank village of Madama bears the names of Palestinians killed in the war. (AP: Majdi Mohammed)

The military criticism appeared to focus on the diversion of resources, rather than the vandalism itself.

The IDF said it viewed the situation with the "utmost severity", and accused Mr Sukkot of "misuse of the protection provided by security forces".

"It should be emphasised that the IDF regularly dismantles symbols of incitement, subject to all required approvals and in coordination with the Civil Administration, as has occurred several times in recent months and and an additional operation is planned for the near future," it said.

"These activities are an important component of the fight against terrorism and incitement to terrorism."

Israel's Prime Minister also condemned the incident — from the perspective of the strain it put on the military.

"The IDF is the sovereign in Judea and Samaria and is responsible for implementing the decisions of the political echelon," Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement.

"Taking the law into its own hands, especially by public figures, is wrong and prevents the IDF from focusing on its missions against terrorism and incitement."

Sukkot previously sanctioned for inciting violence against Palestinians

Zvi Sukkot is a member of the Religious Zionist party, led by right-wing finance minister Bezalel Smotrich — a man who has been sanctioned by the international community, including Australia, for inciting violence against Palestinians.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich leads the country's Religious Zionist Party. (Reuters: Ammar Awad)

Before entering politics, Mr Sukkot had been arrested on allegations of firebombing a mosque.

In 2024, he was among right-wing politicians who encouraged supporters to storm the notorious Sde Teiman detention facility in southern Israel after nine IDF reservists were arrested over the alleged brutal rape of a Palestinian detainee — an incident caught on CCTV, but later dropped by military prosecutors after immense political pressure.

Tensions in the area around Madama have been high in recent weeks, following a deadly shooting attack in the nearby village of Tell.

Two Israeli settlers and four Palestinians were killed in the incident — Israelis accusing the Palestinians of turning on them, while the Palestinians accused the settlers of being armed and aggressive.

The shooting prompted a large scale Israeli military operation in the area, detaining more than 100 Palestinians.

Israeli settlers in the area launched revenge attacks, destroying property and attacking residents.

Israeli media has reported the IDF having warned the Netanyahu government that the surge in settler violence has fuelled tensions in the West Bank, and it was effectively a tinderbox ready to blow.

World.title: Young Australians' home ownership rate at an 80-year low, report shows
World.content:
More young people are abandoning hopes of home ownership amid increasing generational inequality, according to a new report.

Anglicare's Falling Behind report, released on Tuesday, found home ownership among 25-34 year olds has fallen to an 80-year low — highlighting intergenerational inequality from tax settings that favoured housing investment.

Young Australians are facing a future where working hard does not guarantee security, Anglicare Australia executive director Kasy Chambers said after the report's release.

"The economic foundations underneath them have shifted," she said.

Ms Chambers said there was a perfect storm that led to inequality between the generations.

"What we can see is that we've got young people coming into a workforce that is more insecure, we can see that we've got increased costs," she said.

"People are studying longer. We know that it takes much longer to save a deposit for a house in terms of the annual average income versus the deposit."

Kasy Chambers has called for more measures to even the financial playing field. (AAP: Mick Tsikas)

Investment tax breaks fuelling the generational divide

Anglicare's report found older Australians "appear insulated" from today's economic pressures, having earned wages during a stable period in the job market and amassed wealth from investments which are taxed less severely than wages.

The report found that while older Australians' wealth has significantly increased over time, their share of income tax has not.

It said young people are "absorbing the impact" with lower wages proportional to house prices and cost of living — affording less opportunity to amass wealth.

The Albanese government this year introduced tax changes on investments including shares, investment properties and the sale of businesses.

What Labor's tax changes really mean for you Labor's capital gains tax changes have set off a firestorm of debate about the implications for small businesses, start-ups, share owners and plenty more. Here's who will really pay more.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers unveiled the sweeping changes in the May budget, describing them as the "most important and ambitious" reforms in decades, which would make the system "fairer and stronger for workers, businesses, first home buyers and future generations".

Ms Chambers welcomed the federal government's efforts to remove tax breaks for investment income, but said more measures were needed from the federal government to even the playing field.

"We need to look at taxing wealth the same way as income, because otherwise, what we're seeing is that the wealth gets concentrated," she told reporters in Canberra.

"Once it gets concentrated, it's very difficult to share that again ... one dollar is one dollar in taxation terms."

Low welfare payments prevent youth from catching up

Young Australians are eligible for less support from Centrelink despite facing the same costs as older people. (ABC News: Curtis Rodda)

The Anglicare head also called for a shake-up to the Youth Allowance payment, citing the report's findings that young Australians are eligible for less support from Centrelink despite facing the same costs as older people.

How will new unemployment changes affect Centrelink recipients? The federal government has proposed changes to Australia's $2 billion employment services system.

The maximum payment amount for a single person with no children on Youth Allowance is $677.20 a fortnight.

The rate is below the poverty line, JobSeeker and the aged pension, which Ms Chambers said is contributing to generational inequality.

"We have a social security system that literally says a young person needs less money to live on simply because of their age," Ms Chambers said.

"Rent isn't cheaper when you're 23. Groceries aren't cheaper. Electricity isn't cheaper. Yet young people are expected to survive on the lowest payment in the system.

" Poverty should not be a rite of passage. "

The report also highlighted that a single person on JobSeeker falls behind by $251 a week after paying for rent, food and transport — while a single parent on parenting payment falls behind by $174 a week and a couple with two children on JobSeeker falls behind by $428 a week.

It found nearly half of all low-income renters aged under 35 are experiencing rental stress, and not a single rental property across the country was affordable for a single person on the support payment.

ABC/Wires

World.title: Residents killed overnight not far from police station in Haiti
World.content:
A deadly overnight gang raid in a neighbourhood overlooking the Haitian capital, Port-au-Prince, has claimed the lives of 47 people and injured 22 more.

The hillside community of Kenscoff has suffered a dozen attacks by armed gangs since last year, forcing thousands to flee their homes, with the latest raid sparking calls for the police chief to step down.

Hundreds of people have died in gang-related raids in the Haitian neighbourhood of Kenscoff since last year. (Reuters: Patrice Noel)

Haitian rights group RNDDH estimated 30 to 40 people were killed and 15 to 20 wounded in the raid, which began Monday evening around 10:30 pm local time (12:30pm Tuesday AEST), but said it was difficult to assess a complete tally.

Even as Haiti's government decried a "heinous attack" and promised to reinforce security, residents demanded the local police chief step down, saying officers failed to protect people killed just minutes from the police station.

"Kenscoff will not be abandoned," the prime minister's office said on social media.

"The government's authority will be restored without weakness and without delay."

Gang members not counted among the dead

Attacks in Kenscoff over two months in early 2025 saw more than 260 people killed and 200 homes destroyed or set on fire, forcing 3,000 people to flee, according to UN estimates.

Nearly a dozen more attacks have taken place since, including rapes, kidnapping, arson and livestock theft.

"My family are victims," said Coriolan Kendy, standing by his cousin's body, lying on the road in a blood-stained sheet.

"People in Kenscoff are suffering, and the government is to blame."

Some residents said several dozen police had tried to rebuff the armed men during the night, and some were injured.

They added that they did not identify gang members among the dead.

Local media said several houses were set on fire, including the home of Jean William Pape, a leading public health expert.

"The police never gave up," national police chief Vladimir Paraison told reporters during a visit to Kenscoff later in the day.

A house sits damaged after being burned during a deadly overnight raid by an armed gang on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince. (Reuters: Patrice Noel)

Kenscoff overlooks routes into Petion-Ville — home to several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government — as well as a major road from the capital into southern Haiti.

The UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, which is mandated to help police fight gangs, aims to reach a capacity of more than 5,500 troops.

A spokesperson did not immediately respond to questions on whether the troops were reinforcing Kenscoff security.

REUTERS/ABC

World.title: Education union 'blindsided' by ACT public school budget shake-up
World.content:
Public schools in the ACT have received their budgets for next year, with a change in the way their funding is calculated, seeing a number of schools facing a reduction.

The budget shake-up is being made in response to a review of public school resourcing, which found there needed to be more of a focus on equity and student need.

ACT Education Director-General Jo Wood said the independent Public School System Resourcing Review found a significant portion of financial pressures were in primary schools, but the way funding was calculated gave more weight to older students.

Jo Wood says the directorate is commissioning a holistic review of the public school funding formula. (ABC News: Monte Bovill)

"That independent review found one of the pressures on the system and one of the equity issues was the higher weighting that's given to the per-student funding depending on the stage of schooling," Ms Wood said.

"So for example, primary schools get a lower per-student amount than, say, a college.

"The review said we needed to look at that whole funding formula, and we are commissioning a holistic review of that funding formula, but as a first step for 2027 we've made a small adjustment to the weighting for colleges … so that we can get a better distribution of funding across the system."

Eighteen schools will see their funding drop by more than 5 per cent, 31 will see an increase of more than 5 per cent, and 43 schools will receive about the same amount as they did in 2026.

'A significant financial adjustment and a very short turnaround'

Among those worse off are the ACT's nine colleges — which are facing a combined $4 million budget reduction, according to the Australian Education Union (AEU).

AEU ACT branch president Angela Burroughs said some schools had been "blindsided" by the changes.

Angela Burroughs says the scale of the changes to funding for colleges may force them to cut whole programs. (ABC News: Monte Bovill)

"The scale of it, and the way that it's being implemented, is very unexpected," Ms Burroughs said.

"It could be whole programs that have to go. It could be a performing arts program that's no longer viable, or a language education program that's no longer viable.

"It's a significant financial adjustment that college principals need to make, and a very short turnaround time to get ready for 2027."

Executive officer of ACT Parents, Veronica Elliott, said the organisation was "surprised" to learn the 2027 funding changes included a reduction in the funding weighting for colleges.

"The ACT college system is highly valued by families because of the breadth and diversity of courses and pathways available to students," Ms Elliott said.

"We support the objective of greater equity across public education, but changes to college resourcing could affect staffing and the courses colleges are able to offer next year.

"That's particularly important because students have already enrolled and submitted their preferences for 2027."

Veronica Elliott says changes to college resourcing could affect the courses that are able to be offered. (ABC News: Mark Moore)

AEU ACT branch vice-president Simon Vaughan, who is also the principal of an ACT public college, said he did not know what classroom choices his school would be able to offer new year 11 students next year.

"There is a quantum of savings I will have to find," Dr Vaughan said.

"Extracurricular things would probably be areas we need to target.

" And if we have to, for example, cut staff, that may cut programs. "

Ms Wood said the ACT Education Directorate would be offering extra support for schools whose funding was being reduced.

The ACT Education Directorate says it will offer extra support to schools whose funding is being reduced. (ABC News: Luke Stephenson)

"We do have some funding in a central pool that, as we do the work with schools about how they can make those reductions, where there are circumstances that they can't reduce by as much as that, we have the capacity to provide some supplementation," she said.

"And the main thing we want is that people, our principals and school leaders, feel that it's OK to ask for support.

" We're not asking any principal to do this work alone. We are available and have a range of different expertise to provide support. "

Schools will need to finalise their arrangements for 2027 in the coming weeks.

World.title: Crows captain makes tearful speech as All Australian team is named
World.content:
Max Gawn has claimed a record ninth All Australian blazer, while Nick Daicos was named player of the year by both the coaches and his fellow players, but a speech from Adelaide captain Jordan Dawson stole the show at the AFL Awards.

Dawson won Best Captain and Most Courageous Player, before being selected in and named vice captain of the All Australian team, and spoke openly about his mental health on stage.

Dawson's brother died at the age of 35 earlier this year, something he says he has struggled to deal with throughout the season.

"It's been a struggle. It's not easy. It's a range of emotions and they come at different times," Dawson said.

"For me it's about creating safe spaces in the footy club and at home, and understanding there will be times when it's hard to go to work and that it is OK to feel a certain type of way.

"It's still raw, it's always going to be hard to talk about. I'm so lucky I have such supportive people around me.

"The mental health space is something new to me, but something I want to learn more about.

"I want everyone to know who is struggling with their mental health that you are definitely loved and that the world is a better place with you in it. You are enough. We all love you, you have friends and family around you."

Nick Daicos was a multiple winner at the AFL Awards. (Getty Images: Michael Willson)

Gawn, who was named captain of the All Australian side, became the first man to earn nine blazers. Marcus Bontempelli earned selection for an eighth time.

Daicos, selected in the All Australian time for the fourth time in the first five years of his career, also swept the Coaches Association Champion Player of the Year and Leigh Matthews MVP awards.

Carlton's Jagga Smith was named the Rising Star for 2026.

World.title: Luke Gosling charged with breach of bail just weeks after alleged assaults
World.content:
Federal politician Luke Gosling has been charged with breaching his bail conditions, less than a month after he was arrested over allegations he assaulted the Northern Territory Administrator.

In July, the Labor MP was charged with two counts of assault over an alleged incident involving NT Administrator David Connolly at a community event held in Darwin earlier that month.

Mr Gosling is the Commonwealth's special envoy for defence and veterans' affairs, and has held the seat of Solomon — which includes Darwin and its satellite city of Palmerston — since 2016.

The administrator is the Crown's representative in the NT, a vice-regal role equivalent to a state governor.

David Connolly took on the job of Northern Territory Administrator earlier this year. (ABC News: Sam Parry)

Mr Gosling's bail conditions were varied in Darwin Local Court on July 31, with the federal MP banned from coming within 50 metres of the NT's Government House — where Mr Connolly resides.

Judge Stephen Geary also ordered Mr Gosling to give Mr Connolly's office 48 hours' notice before attending any event where both men would be in attendance.

If the two do attend the same event, Mr Gosling is required to stay 15 metres away from the administrator at all times.

In a statement released to media this afternoon, NT Police said Mr Gosling allegedly breached his bail conditions on August 14.

"Today he was served with a summons to appear in Darwin Local Court on 30 September 2026," NT Police said.

Gosling to fight assault charges

In a statement released this evening, a spokesperson for Mr Gosling said no details had been shared by police regarding the alleged breach.

Last month, Luke Gosling faced Darwin Local Court where he was granted bail. (ABC News: Matilda Colling)

"Neither Mr Gosling nor his office have been made aware of the nature of the alleged breach and have been provided no information from police other than a summons," the spokesperson said.

"On Friday, August 14 Mr Gosling did not attend any events at the same time as the administrator.

"Mr Gosling is discussing the matter with his legal team, and will be defending the charge."

The statement said Mr Gosling's office would not comment further "as the matter is before the court", listed to be heard on September 30.

During Mr Gosling's first court appearance, the court heard the assault charges related to two separate incidents which allegedly occurred 30 minutes apart.

Luke Gosling to be prosecuted by Commonwealth DPP The Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions is set to take over the case against Federal Labor MP Luke Gosling, to avoid a perceived conflict of interest within the Northern Territory Director of Public Prosecutions.

In discussing the reported details, Mr Gosling's lawyer Marty Aust SC told the court the first alleged incident had occurred "in a manner in which the administrator was unable to see the approach".

The court heard the second charge pertained to an alleged hip-and-shoulder collision between the two men, during which Mr Gosling allegedly drew back his left elbow and struck Mr Connolly in his upper rib.

Mr Gosling has strenuously denied the assault allegations, with his lawyer previously telling media the charges would be contested in court.

The federal MP has faced pressure to step down from his political role since news broke of the alleged assault, including from Shadow Defence Minister James Paterson and NT Senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price.

Federal Opposition Leader Angus Taylor urged Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to stand down the Solomon MP.

In a statement released after news broke of the fresh charge, Angus Taylor urged the prime minister to stand down the Solomon MP. (ABC News: Matt Roberts)

"When these serious charges were first laid, we said this was a test of the prime minister's leadership and Luke Gosling should be stood down from his special envoy role while the matter is dealt with," Mr Taylor said in a statement released this afternoon.

"Now Mr Gosling has also been charged with allegedly breaching his bail, the case for the prime minister to act is even stronger.

"These allegations are matters for the courts, but Anthony Albanese has a decision to make about who serves in his government. He should stand Mr Gosling down today."

But Mr Albanese has doubled down on his earlier stance, claiming again this evening that it would be inappropriate to comment while legal proceedings play out.

"There is a legal process underway. No further comment at this time," a spokesperson for the prime minister said.

World.title: Distress beacon borrowing program proposed after teen hiker's death
World.content:
A New South Wales mayor has described Lily Hooper as an amazing woman full of spirit and adventure who was taken too soon, while promising to establish a bushwalking safety program in her honour.

The 18-year-old's body was found in bushland of the Nattai National Park, near Mittagong, last Thursday after an eight-day search.

Almost 1,000 people from multiple agencies took part in the search when she did not return from her solo hike on the Bonnen Pic Walking Trail.

The cause of her death is not yet known, but NSW Police have said her body was located a significant distance from the path.

Wollondilly Shire Council held a minute's silence at its council meeting on Tuesday afternoon.

Mayor Matt Gould said the council would collaborate with NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service to make bushwalking safety equipment more readily available.

Lily Hooper, 18, went missing while hiking in Nattai National Park. (Supplied: NSW Police)

"I've spoken with Lily's family about how our community might permanently remember her," Cr Gould said during council's ordinary meeting on Wednesday.

"Rather than creating a single physical memorial … we will establish a program in Lily's memory where council purchases personal locator beacons and makes them available for residents and bushwalkers to borrow free of charge, alongside practical bushwalking safety information.

"A personal locator beacon is something you hope nobody ever needs to activate, but if someone does find themselves in trouble in remote country, having one can make an enormous difference.

"My hope is that this becomes a living and practical legacy in Lily's name, something that helps people enjoy the bush safely."

Matt Gould says the community's response to Lily Hooper's death has been overwhelming. (ABC News)

Cr Gould also thanked emergency crews involved in the search for Ms Hooper and said there had been an enormous outpouring of community grief.

"While most of us never knew Lily personally, I think over the past two weeks, our community has come to understand just how special she was through the people who did," he said.

Purple lights, flags lowered

Tributes left in memory of Ms Hooper at Oakdale's Willis Park, south west of Sydney, have been carefully collected after the town was hit by wet weather.

With the support of her family, council staff gathered some of the cards and signs on Monday to protect them from rain.

The items have been passed on to the Hoopers, with the memorial space to remain open to the community until Friday.

An outpouring of grief has followed the death of bushwalker Lily Hooper. (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

Just hours after Ms Hooper's body was found, Wollondilly Performing Arts Centre was lit up purple and the council chamber's flags flown at half mast.

Ms Hooper's former school, Campelltown Performing Arts High School, posted an online tribute, describing their 2025 graduate as a kind, humorous and respectful young woman.

"[She] lit up every room with her infectious smile, positive energy and determination to live life to the full," the post read.

"This loss has had a significant impact on our students, staff and wider school community."

Meanwhile, a fundraiser organised by the Rotary Club of Wollondilly North in support of the Hooper family has raised a growing $30,000.

Dozens of community members, friends and family have flocked to Oakdale's Willis Park to pay their respects to Lily Hooper. (ABC Illawarra: Justin Huntsdale)

State government honour

NSW Premier Chris Minns on Monday promised to work with Ms Hooper's family on a special tribute to honour her.

Her father, Jim Hooper, told 7NEWS he would like the flag on the Sydney Harbour Bridge lowered as she worked as a Bridge Climb tour guide.

"I want to talk with them and work on it together, but we'll do something special for Lily and frankly it's the least we can do," Mr Minns said.

" It's a terrible life lost and it's a lovely family. "

NSW Deputy Premier Prue Car said on Sunday the government was open to reviewing safety signage in national parks to prevent deaths like Ms Hooper's.

"We are open to ideas on that. We are constantly saying to people, 'Try and get your kids off their phones and into nature,' but we have to make sure we are making that are safe as possible," she said.

Lily Hooper went missing is in rugged terrain south of Sydney. (Supplied: NSW National Parks)

The comments come just days after Mr Minns vowed to apologise in person to Ms Hooper's family after he told parliament their daughter was found alive.

"I'm also absolutely devastated and profoundly sorry that anything I said may have added to the grief that that family has gone through," Mr Minns said on Friday.

Emergency services are examining whether a miscommunication about a police code may have led to Ms Hooper being incorrectly identified as alive.

A coronial investigation is also underway.

World.title: ‘What people don’t realise’: Candid Hird opens up after missing out on the Essendon coaching role
World.content:
Analysis SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘What people don’t realise’: Candid Hird opens up after missing out on the Essendon coaching role Jon Pierik Updated August 25, 2026 — 10:47pm ,first published 11:51am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

When James Hird said his goodbyes after finishing his challenging interview before the panel charged with finding Essendon’s new coach, he was buoyant. On two fronts. According to a senior industry figure with knowledge of the Bombers’ interviewing process, the former premiership captain and club great felt as if he had done all he could to reclaim a role he cherished, and one he had held proudly more than a decade ago before trouble struck. Mark McVeigh (left) and James Hird with the Bombers in 2004. Getty Images But, just as importantly, he was also satisfied the Bombers had run a thorough process, where he was given the freedom to push his case, but – on the flipside – was spared no leniency. That’s why, amid the disappointment of being overlooked in favour of great mate Mark McVeigh, Hird cannot complain.



“From a personal point of view though, it’s very disappointing,” Hird said on Nine’s Footy Furnace after it was confirmed that he, like Fremantle assistant Jaymie Graham and Adelaide coaching director Murray Davis, had missed out on the job. “Yeah, I’m disappointed, put my heart and soul into the effort, but, obviously, fell short and that’s the way it goes.” Loading On Tuesday night’s episode of Footy Classified (also on Nine), Hird spoke about the Essendon coach selection process and detailed part of an “off-the-record” conversation with club president, and former teammate, Andrew Welsh, who according to Hird told him the process would be genuine, and the Brownlow and Norm Smith medallist was “definitely not at the front of the queue” heading into it. After McVeigh said at his introductory press conference that he loved Hird, and that the two are close friends, Hird expanded further.



“We’ve been friends for 27 years, since he walked in the doors in 1999 to the Essendon Football Club,” he said. “[I’m] incredibly proud of Mark – a wonderful person, great mate, and I couldn’t be prouder. “What people don’t realise is that the last four weeks we’ve been going through this interview process together. We’ve spoken every day over the last four or five weeks about the process, ‘What questions did you get?’, ‘What questions did I get?’ “He’s going to do an incredible job, and I just hope all Essendon people get behind him.” Loading



Before facing the selection committee of chief executive Tim Roberts, Welsh, vice president Anthony Di Pietro, board member and former Swans player Ted Richards and people and culture executive Caroline Monzon, Hird had felt the one issue that may torpedo his bid to return was the hangover from the supplements’ saga all those years ago, the senior industry figure said. Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘Unite behind our club’: Powerbroker’s call for peace as McVeigh appointed Essendon coach However, Hird felt he had moved on as best he could. McVeigh was one of the 34 players suspended for the 2016 season. Over the years since, Hird has met with many of the 34 who had sought answers, and Hird provided them with as much clarity as he could. There were a couple who still harboured frustration, but Hird, according to the same senior source, had left those deep conversations believing the two parties were now on better terms. This process was relayed to Welsh when he asked Hird about his relationships with those former players, according to the source.



Hird, himself, backed this up on Tuesday night, adding, “some bridges have been mended through the process – some people through the ASADA saga that we sort of headbutted and fought [against], I’ve come back together with them ... there’s been a lot of positives gone on through this process, but as I said it’s time to get behind Mark and the football club and go forward.” Welsh declined to discuss specifics of the interview when asked about this on Tuesday. “I’m not going to go into specifics of candidates. What I will go into is that Murray [Davis], James and Jaymie [Graham] were all fantastic, and all had different views on different things from a game-style perspective, and also from a club perspective, but I won’t be commenting on any questions that we did or didn’t ask any of those candidates,” Welsh said. Hird was pushed and challenged through the Bombers’ detailed process, as were all the candidates. Late in his pivotal interview, Hird, according to two sources with knowledge of the meeting, asked the panel: “What concerns have you got about me being the coach?”



Hird and McVeigh at Essendon in 2010. Getty Images Roberts said he had wondered whether Hird was “bigger than the club”. But Roberts and the rest of the panel agreed in the end that their concerns on that front had been extinguished. Ted Richards, the club’s football director, and a former teammate who went on to be a Sydney Swans’ premiership player, told Hird that successful coaches typically come from a top-four or top-six team and had experience at multiple clubs. Hird did not. Hird politely reminded the questioner that he had been captain of the best team of his era, the dominant 2000 premiership side, and, in his first stint as coach, the Bombers had played off for top spot on the ladder in round 14, 2013. As this masthead has reported, Hird has also made it clear he has been involved in high-performance environments in the years since, including the business world, and you don’t need to follow the “typical linear” model to succeed.



Hird had briefly been an assistant coach at GWS when McVeigh was caretaker coach, and is now director of coaching at VFL club, Port Melbourne. He had seen how the game – and coaching – had changed, the attention span of younger players becoming shorter and shorter in this modern, social media-driven age. Rather than long sermons, Hird had seen the importance of soundbites, and the use of artificial intelligence. Hird was asked how he would handle major media issues. The panel acknowledged that what Hird said, because of his huge standing in the game, let alone the club, carried tremendous weight, so if he broke ranks, the club could be destabilised. Hird responded that he would always consult the president and chief executive, and would fall into line behind what the club wanted, regardless of his own view.



Andrew Welsh (second from left) and McVeigh (second from right) in their playing days. Paul Rovere Soccer great Kevin Muscat was used by the Bombers to scrutinise the applicants’ game plan and strategy, although this was an open-ended question because applicants needed more details on the opponent they may have been playing and conditions at the venue. Related Article AFL briefing

AFL 2026 United Dons vow no ‘jumping at shadows’ now that McVeigh has top job For anyone who has listened to Hird weekly on his football shows on Nine, the owner of this masthead, he has been big on having a team outnumber an opponent at the contest, and then run, spread and attack – as is the modern way. However, Welsh said McVeigh had the better plan. “Mark was clearly the best candidate for what this role demands. He’s developed emerging talent throughout his coaching career, and he connects with younger players in a way that matters for a list at our stage,” Welsh said.



“His game plan is built for the modern game, quick ball movement, adaptable structures, and it’s suited to where this competition is heading.” Hird believed he was the best applicant for the job. As did all the applicants; otherwise, why would they have applied? The Bombers may yet seek to bring him back inside the tent in a prominent role, but Hird craved the senior coaching role, and may be unwilling. Welsh said on Tuesday he was keen to catch up with Hird and would love to see him at Essendon in some capacity. Hird later explained on Footy Classified, “I’ll get round to ringing Andrew, but in my mind there’s no rush, I mean today’s about Mark and about the Essendon Football Club, and what Mark wants to do going forward with the club”. A twist in the tale would be if Hird joined another club, having raised eyebrows on Sunday when he said rivals had reached out to him. Hird has repeatedly said he wants what’s best for the Bombers, a one-time power that has fallen on hard and miserable times and just completed its worst season. As former club president Lindsay Tanner said, the job of all Essendon people now is to unite behind the new coach. Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: No Cripps, no Newcombe: Biggest All-Australian snubs revealed
World.content:
Newly minted All-Australian captain Max Gawn has spoken passionately about the leadership of Jordan Dawson, the Adelaide skipper who gave a spine-tingling speech earlier in the night.

Dawson was named Gawn’s vice-captain in this year’s 23-man All-Australian team. But it was Dawson’s message about the importance of mental health after he tragically lost his older brother Jaryd Dawson during the year that was the most telling.

Jordan Dawson and Max Gawn. AFL Photos

“I think we saw leadership tonight,” Gawn said.

“I think for Jordan to get up and do what he did, to speak about mental health, to lead his side through the tragedy that happened to his family. And then to show vulnerability in front of a group of strangers that he hasn’t got it right, he hasn’t got it perfect with his battle right now, and asking for help – like that’s a captain that I want to be behind.”

The veteran Melbourne captain even half-joked that he was thankful for the “gesture” of being named captain of the AFL’s best team.

“So I appreciate the gesture, but I want to get behind Jordan Dawson, and I want to allow him to do the speech, because his speech was perfect tonight,” Gawn said.

Support is available from Beyond Blue on 1300 22 4636 and Lifeline on 13 11 14.

World.title: Beijing warns it will not sever ties with Iran after US vows ‘economic D-Day’
World.content:
WorldAsiaTrade wars Beijing warns it will not sever ties with Iran after US vows ‘economic D-Day’ Lisa Visentin August 25, 2026 — 10:25pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Beijing: China has fired a warning shot at Washington, making clear it won’t cease cooperating with Iran and was prepared to retaliate if the Trump administration continued with fresh sanctions. In a move that sets up another potential collision course with Beijing, US Treasury Scott Bessent this week declared an “economic D-Day” on Iran, seeking to sever its remaining financial lifelines by hitting collaborators with sanctions. Beijing responded on Tuesday by defending its ties with Tehran, and warning it would not bow down to US pressure. Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are expected to meet for a high-stakes summit at the White House next month. Getty “China’s cooperation with Iran has always been conducted within the international framework and should not be interfered with or undermined,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said at a press conference in Beijing.



Related Article Analysis

Middle East at war The White House says this is the Iran endgame. We’ve heard that before “China is closely monitoring relevant developments and will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own interests.” China buys as much as 90 per cent of Iran’s oil, providing Tehran with a critical source of revenue that helps sustain the Islamic regime in the face of crippling sanctions. Any move by the US to truly strangle Iran’s finances would have to take aim at its trade ties with China, and in particular, the Chinese banks processing oil payment transactions. Such an escalation would almost certainly blow up the fragile trade truce struck between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last year, and derail the leaders’ high-stakes summit at the White House next month, something both Beijing and Washington have otherwise appeared intent on avoiding.



The Trump administration has given few details about exactly how it will economically decapitate Iran, other than broadly threaten foreign entities with exclusion from the US financial system if they continued to do business with Tehran. Related Article Updated

Middle East at war US launches ‘Operation Economic Outcast’ to isolate Iran from the world While declaring that no country would be exempt, Bessent made clear the US was not prepared to go after the Chinese banks. “We are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behaviour. Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?” he said on Monday (US time). Meanwhile, the US Treasury Department unveiled a package of fresh sanctions against 60 entities, including logistics and shipping companies based in Hong Kong and mainland China, but it avoided targeting major Chinese financial institutions.



China has condemned the sanctions as unilateral measures that will only worsen conflicts and called for a return to negotiations. Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: Gawn enjoys a blazing All-Australian run but makes passionate speech for rival skipper
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 Gawn enjoys a blazing All-Australian run but makes passionate speech for rival skipper Jon Pierik August 25, 2026 — 9:37pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Melbourne captain Max Gawn has capped a record ninth All-Australian selection by being named captain, but the biggest moment of the night came when his Adelaide counterpart Jordan Dawson was named to the side for the third time. On the field, the Crows skipper had a year to remember, but off-field he endured unimaginable heartbreak with the loss of his elder brother, Jaryd. Jonathan Brown interviews Max Gawn in one of the moments of the night at Centrepiece at Melbourne Park. AFL Photos In paying tribute to Dawson, Gawn said he knew who showed the most leadership this season – the No.12 for Adelaide. “I think we saw leadership tonight,” Gawn said.



“For Jordan to get up and do what he did, to lead his side … to show vulnerability in front of a group of strangers … that’s a captain that I want to be behind.” Earlier, Dawson – this year’s All-Australian vice captain – gave a spine-tingling speech about the importance of speaking up when times are tough. View post on X “I just want to wish anyone who’s struggled with mental health out there, or who is struggling with mental health, to know you are loved, and the world is a better place with you in it” On the football front, there were several controversial omissions in the 23-man team unveiled on Tuesday night.



Gawn became the first man to earn nine green blazers and was honoured to also assume the captaincy, a role Demons coach Steven King last week said he deserved. Gawn had captained the All-Australian side once before, in 2021. Record breaker: Melbourne captain Max Gawn has received his ninth All-Australian blazer. AFL Photos Western Bulldogs counterpart Marcus Bontempelli joined a select group of eight – Gary Ablett snr, Gary Ablett jnr, Patrick Dangerfield, Lance Franklin, Robert Harvey and Mark Ricciuto – to have enjoyed the top honour eight times. A record five Indigenous players were named – Wayne Milera, Jarman Impey, Kysaiah Pickett, Shai Bolton and Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera. The record had been four players in 2006, when Shaun Burgoyne, Lindsay Gilbee, Adam Goodes and Andrew McLeod were honoured. Loading



The club-imposed suspension of Sydney players Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner – almost certainly all would have been selected – opened up three spots, but there were still contentious selections. Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 Butters declares he’s leaving Port, but he won’t get to Collingwood. Suns spearhead also on the move Zak Butters, despite playing only 17 games because of injury, was chosen ahead of Hawthorn co-captain Jai Newcombe, and Carlton superstar Patrick Cripps, who has been integral to the Blues’ rise under Josh Fraser. Port Adelaide defender Aliir Aliir was also a surprise omission, while teammate Jason Horne-Francis also had strong claims. Geelong wingman Oliver Dempsey was one of nine maiden All-Australians, the young star redefining how his role is played through his ability to push forward and kick goals. However, Dempsey was chosen ahead of star teammate Max Holmes, who was in superb touch, averaging 29 disposals, before a right ankle fracture and syndesmosis injury in July.



Emerging Fremantle gun Murphy Reid donned a blazer in just his second year in the AFL, an outstanding achievement. All told, 10 players retained their spots from the 2025 team – Gawn, Bontempelli, Dawson, Wanganeen-Milera, Pickett, Jordan Clark, Harris Andrews, Bailey Smith, Zac Bailey and Nick Daicos. The full list of club representation was: Adelaide (two), Brisbane Lions (three), Collingwood (one), Fremantle (five), Geelong (two), GWS (one), Hawthorn (two), Melbourne (two), Port Adelaide (one), St Kilda (two), Sydney Swans (one) and Western Bulldogs (one). The selection panel included AFL CEO Andrew Dillon (chair), Eddie Betts, Simon Black, Jude Bolton, Abbey Holmes, Glen Jakovich, Laura Kane, David Mundy, Joel Selwood and Greg Swann.



Meanwhile, Daicos, now a three-time All Australian, was crowned the AFL Players’ Association most valuable player for a second time, capping a fine season in which he polled 147 votes – a new benchmark. Daicos, having averaged a whopping 35 disposals per game, beat Bontempelli (109 votes) and Gawn (99) to the honour. He also won the award in 2024. He surpassed Richmond champion Dustin Martin’s previous benchmark of 122 votes in 2017. “We are incredibly proud of what he has achieved and even more so for the way he approaches his game in all phases. On-field and off-field, Nick sets the standard at our club and is a wonderful leader. We want our program not just to develop great players, but incredible people and Nick really represents that,” Magpies coach Craig McRae said. St Kilda co-captain Callum Wilkie claimed the inaugural AFL Coaches Association defensive player of the year. World.title: PM, corporate titans flock to Sofitel for Business Council dinner
World.content:
NationalCBD Opinion PM, corporate titans flock to Sofitel for Business Council dinner John Buckley CBD columnist Updated August 25, 2026 — 8:23pm , first published 7:35pm

Updated August 25, 2026 — 8:23pm ,first published 7:35pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Few events in business and politics get the high-calibre turnout that the Business Council of Australia’s annual dinner has come to deliver. And that’s before factoring in the will-he-won’t-he speculation over whether Commonwealth Bank chief executive Matt Comyn would be among the major corporates to show face for the get-together at the Sofitel hotel in Sydney’s CBD on Tuesday evening. (To our surprise, Comyn was there.) Keynote address: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the BCA dinner. Janie Barrett The guest list had no shortage of talent. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese was billed as the headline guest, with a gaggle of senior Labor figures in tow. Also from the government, Trade Minister Don Farrell showed up to mingle with execs ahead of dinner, as did Assistant Science, Technology and Digital Economy Minister Andrew Charlton, and Assistant Productivity Minister Andrew Leigh, who, if our eyes didn’t deceive us, arrived to the ballroom with his backpack slung over his shoulder.



Man of the moment: CBA head honcho Matt Comyn. Janie Barrett Money man: Daniel Mookhey, Treasurer of NSW. Janie Barrett NAB chief economist Dr Sally Auld. Oscar Colman But if reporting from our colleagues on Monday was any indicator, Albanese was no doubt bracing for a tough crowd. The star-studded audience was led by BCA chief executive Bran Black, who was preparing to send the government a warning shot on productivity, according to speech notes reported by this masthead. Our guess is that Black will have no shortage of backers for his message. The top executives of Australia’s biggest companies were expected to turn out in force for the annual get-together, including Telstra chief executive Vicki Brady, Coles chief Leah Weckert and representatives from the big four banks.



Apart from Comyn, the bankers included NAB chairman Philip Chronican, who was on the list but whom we didn’t get eyes on, as well as Westpac chief Anthony Miller and ANZ’s still-relatively-new CEO Nuno Matos. Also expected were Citi chief executive Mark Woodruff and Macquarie boss ⁠Stuart Green. Related Article Exclusive

Political leadership Albanese tells Queensland to get with the program on AI revolution The Minns government was represented, with NSW Treasurer Daniel Mookhey firmly ensconced. Public servants were also well represented. ASIC chair Sarah Court and ACCC chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb were each set to turn out for the function, as was Steven Kennedy, secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, and Treasury secretary Jenny Wilkinson. Jan Adams, secretary of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, was also expected to go along, as was Department of Climate Change and Energy secretary Mike Kaiser.



Bondi Partners founding partner and president Joe Hockey (left) and Business Council of Australia president Geoff Culbert. Oscar Colman As with all of these types of functions, there is always a reliable turnout from the hangers-on. So it was little surprise to see former federal treasurer turned Trump whisperer Joe Hockey back on the list this year, along with former defence minister Christopher Pyne. The pair were among the eager and enthusiastic who turned up unfashionably early. (Those relationships aren’t going to cultivate themselves.) Christopher Pyne is in the house. Oscar Colman AirTrunk founder Robin Khuda, APA Group chief Adam Watson, and AGL Energy boss Damien Nicks. Janie Barrett Jodie Haydon and husband Anthony Albanese are greeted by Bran Black. Oscar Colman



AGL Energy chief executive officer Damien Nicks (left) and Mirvac group chief executive officer and managing director Campbell Hanan. Oscar Colman Chris Bowen flirts with Murdoch’s son-in-law Earlier this month, Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen slipped into a flannelette overshirt and stared down what we’d assume was an iPhone camera to talk up how the government is making it easier for farmers to go solar. Related Article Farming How Rupert Murdoch’s son-in-law solved crisis at family farm As part of the roadshow, Bowen met with board members of Growing Australia’s Nature Economy, otherwise known as “GANE”. So far, so unremarkable. But it was the name of another high-profile Australian who appeared on the minister’s register of interests, days later, that piqued our interest: Alasdair MacLeod.



The man would need no introduction to our good friends over at Holt Street. That’s because this is the same Alasdair MacLeod, Bowen’s office confirmed, who is married to Prudence MacLeod, the eldest daughter of none other than Rupert Murdoch. MacLeod, according to Bowen’s disclosure, hosted the minister as a guest at his home for a night following a tour of carbon farming initiatives. Bowen, we’re told, dropped in on MacLeod’s farm in Yass for a two-day seminar that brought together experts in wildlife, conservation, agricultural science and climate to talk about how farmers can get more income out of soil carbon capture. (How fun!) Prue and Alasdair MacLeod are big nature, agriculture and climate action enthusiasts. In 2019, the pair founded the Macdoch Foundation, which, at least according to its website, has invested extended philanthropic grants worth $44.5 million to 65 organisations. But something tells us the couple’s love of nature isn’t the only reason Bowen might be feeling pleased with himself. World.title: Essendon claim heritage was not a factor, but McVeigh’s return feels like a homecoming
World.content:
Analysis SportAFLAFL 2026 Essendon claim heritage was not a factor, but McVeigh’s return feels like a homecoming Andrew Wu August 25, 2026 — 8:12pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Despite Essendon president Andrew Welsh’s insistence that Mark McVeigh’s Bombers heritage had little bearing on his appointment as coach, his unveiling could not have felt more like a homecoming. Just days after the club secured just their second wooden spoon in 93 years, there was a buoyant mood at “the Hangar” for McVeigh’s coronation in front of the Bombers’ entire men’s and women’s lists. They gave him a rousing ovation as he entered the stage. Mark McVeigh is Essendon’s new coach. The Age “It’s a great day for the Essendon Football Club,” Welsh opened. “Mark, congratulations! We’re rapt to have you back in the red and black.” Coaching announcements are significant moments for a football club, marking the start of what they hope is a new and more prosperous era, but the reaction to McVeigh’s selection, or rather James Hird’s non-selection, has been mixed among the Essendon constituents.



For elements of the supporter base, all yearning for a return to the days of glory and fame, Hird is still revered as the club’s most recent premiership captain and the face of their last golden era despite his role in the drugs saga that crippled the club in the 2010s. Related Article AFL briefing

AFL 2026 United Dons vow no ‘jumping at shadows’ now that McVeigh has top job McVeigh is no Hird but, given his 232-game career as a heart-and-soul Bomber, has the record to cut through among the more nostalgic of the red-and-black faithful. What McVeigh lacked on his playing resume compared to Hird, he more than made up for with his coaching CV. Like Josh Fraser, appointed at Carlton with contrastingly minimal fanfare a week earlier, McVeigh has completed an extensive apprenticeship.



As Hird ventured into the business world and dipped his toes in the coaching waters at AFL expansion club GWS and Port Melbourne in the VFL, McVeigh immersed himself in just about every aspect of coaching at the Giants and Sydney. Leaving home daily at 4am for the 90-minute commute to Sydney, McVeigh has served as an interim, been a long-time assistant and also coached juniors, the latter significant as he takes the helm of one of the youngest lists in the league. Loading “Our members, our fans, and our club wanted us to set out with a very rigorous process to undertake to find what is the best coach for our football club,” Welsh said. “That went all the way back to looking at what a success profile looked like for the best candidate as a coach. “Understanding the Essendon Football Club, or being an Essendon person, was something that wasn’t held in as high regard internally with the panel that it was externally with some of the commentary going around.”



There is no time for McVeigh to get his feet under the table. The Bombers are an issues-rich club. Related Article Analysis

AFL 2026 ‘What people don’t realise’: Candid Hird opens up after missing out on the Essendon coaching role He will meet with Zach Merrett, who watched the announcement with his teammates, “at an appropriate time” to discuss the former captain’s future. Welsh was adamant 12 months ago Merrett would remain a Bomber in 2026. McVeigh adopted a more conciliatory tone about 2027. He was non-committal when asked if he would attempt to persuade Merrett to stay should his heart still be set on leaving. “You must respect your champions, I’m big on that,” McVeigh said.



“I think it’s really important we understand the players’ feelings. It’s not just about the club’s feelings. It’s about his feelings and where he’s at. I respect him. I want him to be here, but I’ll listen to him as well.” Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘Put my heart and soul into it’: Hird disappointed as Dons prepare to endorse McVeigh as coach He was unequivocal about his great mate Dean Solomon, laughing off reports of tension between the pair. Solomon was among the throng watching on. “I absolutely want Dean Solomon as part of the group,” McVeigh said. But the spectre of Hird still hovers. Welsh and McVeigh know how deeply Hird is loved, not just by the rank and file but the high net worth supporters. Both Welsh and McVeigh called for unity.



“I want to call out the Essendon armada, the thousands of supporters, members, and coteries,” McVeigh said. “I don’t ask for your patience. I ask for your realignment to our club. This is a significant day for our football club, and I can’t wait to start.” Loading Pointedly, Hird was yet to return Welsh’s calls before the announcement but, according to McVeigh, was warm in his congratulations of the new coach. Despite Hird’s affection for McVeigh, only wins will silence those who want the former golden boy to get his crack at redemption. “I don’t fear those people. I actually embrace how they feel, and I understand it,” McVeigh said. “To be fair, he’s been a constant in my life since I was 17 years of age. And we spoke this morning, and the way he spoke to me of how proud [he is] of this moment for me – it hasn’t broken us.



“We’re still together, but I understand, and I embrace the feelings of people that love James Hird because I do, too.” Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: ‘What people don’t realise’: Candid Hird opens up after missing out on the Essendon coaching role
World.content:
Analysis SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘What people don’t realise’: Candid Hird opens up after missing out on the Essendon coaching role Jon Pierik Updated August 25, 2026 — 10:47pm ,first published 11:51am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

When James Hird said his goodbyes after finishing his challenging interview before the panel charged with finding Essendon’s new coach, he was buoyant. On two fronts. According to a senior industry figure with knowledge of the Bombers’ interviewing process, the former premiership captain and club great felt as if he had done all he could to reclaim a role he cherished, and one he had held proudly more than a decade ago before trouble struck. Mark McVeigh (left) and James Hird with the Bombers in 2004. Getty Images But, just as importantly, he was also satisfied the Bombers had run a thorough process, where he was given the freedom to push his case, but – on the flipside – was spared no leniency. That’s why, amid the disappointment of being overlooked in favour of great mate Mark McVeigh, Hird cannot complain.



“From a personal point of view though, it’s very disappointing,” Hird said on Nine’s Footy Furnace after it was confirmed that he, like Fremantle assistant Jaymie Graham and Adelaide coaching director Murray Davis, had missed out on the job. “Yeah, I’m disappointed, put my heart and soul into the effort, but, obviously, fell short and that’s the way it goes.” Loading On Tuesday night’s episode of Footy Classified (also on Nine), Hird spoke about the Essendon coach selection process and detailed part of an “off-the-record” conversation with club president, and former teammate, Andrew Welsh, who according to Hird told him the process would be genuine, and the Brownlow and Norm Smith medallist was “definitely not at the front of the queue” heading into it. After McVeigh said at his introductory press conference that he loved Hird, and that the two are close friends, Hird expanded further.



“We’ve been friends for 27 years, since he walked in the doors in 1999 to the Essendon Football Club,” he said. “[I’m] incredibly proud of Mark – a wonderful person, great mate, and I couldn’t be prouder. “What people don’t realise is that the last four weeks we’ve been going through this interview process together. We’ve spoken every day over the last four or five weeks about the process, ‘What questions did you get?’, ‘What questions did I get?’ “He’s going to do an incredible job, and I just hope all Essendon people get behind him.” Loading



Before facing the selection committee of chief executive Tim Roberts, Welsh, vice president Anthony Di Pietro, board member and former Swans player Ted Richards and people and culture executive Caroline Monzon, Hird had felt the one issue that may torpedo his bid to return was the hangover from the supplements’ saga all those years ago, the senior industry figure said. Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘Unite behind our club’: Powerbroker’s call for peace as McVeigh appointed Essendon coach However, Hird felt he had moved on as best he could. McVeigh was one of the 34 players suspended for the 2016 season. Over the years since, Hird has met with many of the 34 who had sought answers, and Hird provided them with as much clarity as he could. There were a couple who still harboured frustration, but Hird, according to the same senior source, had left those deep conversations believing the two parties were now on better terms. This process was relayed to Welsh when he asked Hird about his relationships with those former players, according to the source.



Hird, himself, backed this up on Tuesday night, adding, “some bridges have been mended through the process – some people through the ASADA saga that we sort of headbutted and fought [against], I’ve come back together with them ... there’s been a lot of positives gone on through this process, but as I said it’s time to get behind Mark and the football club and go forward.” Welsh declined to discuss specifics of the interview when asked about this on Tuesday. “I’m not going to go into specifics of candidates. What I will go into is that Murray [Davis], James and Jaymie [Graham] were all fantastic, and all had different views on different things from a game-style perspective, and also from a club perspective, but I won’t be commenting on any questions that we did or didn’t ask any of those candidates,” Welsh said. Hird was pushed and challenged through the Bombers’ detailed process, as were all the candidates. Late in his pivotal interview, Hird, according to two sources with knowledge of the meeting, asked the panel: “What concerns have you got about me being the coach?”



Hird and McVeigh at Essendon in 2010. Getty Images Roberts said he had wondered whether Hird was “bigger than the club”. But Roberts and the rest of the panel agreed in the end that their concerns on that front had been extinguished. Ted Richards, the club’s football director, and a former teammate who went on to be a Sydney Swans’ premiership player, told Hird that successful coaches typically come from a top-four or top-six team and had experience at multiple clubs. Hird did not. Hird politely reminded the questioner that he had been captain of the best team of his era, the dominant 2000 premiership side, and, in his first stint as coach, the Bombers had played off for top spot on the ladder in round 14, 2013. As this masthead has reported, Hird has also made it clear he has been involved in high-performance environments in the years since, including the business world, and you don’t need to follow the “typical linear” model to succeed.



Hird had briefly been an assistant coach at GWS when McVeigh was caretaker coach, and is now director of coaching at VFL club, Port Melbourne. He had seen how the game – and coaching – had changed, the attention span of younger players becoming shorter and shorter in this modern, social media-driven age. Rather than long sermons, Hird had seen the importance of soundbites, and the use of artificial intelligence. Hird was asked how he would handle major media issues. The panel acknowledged that what Hird said, because of his huge standing in the game, let alone the club, carried tremendous weight, so if he broke ranks, the club could be destabilised. Hird responded that he would always consult the president and chief executive, and would fall into line behind what the club wanted, regardless of his own view.



Andrew Welsh (second from left) and McVeigh (second from right) in their playing days. Paul Rovere Soccer great Kevin Muscat was used by the Bombers to scrutinise the applicants’ game plan and strategy, although this was an open-ended question because applicants needed more details on the opponent they may have been playing and conditions at the venue. Related Article AFL briefing

AFL 2026 United Dons vow no ‘jumping at shadows’ now that McVeigh has top job For anyone who has listened to Hird weekly on his football shows on Nine, the owner of this masthead, he has been big on having a team outnumber an opponent at the contest, and then run, spread and attack – as is the modern way. However, Welsh said McVeigh had the better plan. “Mark was clearly the best candidate for what this role demands. He’s developed emerging talent throughout his coaching career, and he connects with younger players in a way that matters for a list at our stage,” Welsh said.



“His game plan is built for the modern game, quick ball movement, adaptable structures, and it’s suited to where this competition is heading.” Hird believed he was the best applicant for the job. As did all the applicants; otherwise, why would they have applied? The Bombers may yet seek to bring him back inside the tent in a prominent role, but Hird craved the senior coaching role, and may be unwilling. Welsh said on Tuesday he was keen to catch up with Hird and would love to see him at Essendon in some capacity. Hird later explained on Footy Classified, “I’ll get round to ringing Andrew, but in my mind there’s no rush, I mean today’s about Mark and about the Essendon Football Club, and what Mark wants to do going forward with the club”. A twist in the tale would be if Hird joined another club, having raised eyebrows on Sunday when he said rivals had reached out to him. Hird has repeatedly said he wants what’s best for the Bombers, a one-time power that has fallen on hard and miserable times and just completed its worst season. As former club president Lindsay Tanner said, the job of all Essendon people now is to unite behind the new coach. Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: No Cripps, no Newcombe: Biggest All-Australian snubs revealed
World.content:
Newly minted All-Australian captain Max Gawn has spoken passionately about the leadership of Jordan Dawson, the Adelaide skipper who gave a spine-tingling speech earlier in the night.

Dawson was named Gawn’s vice-captain in this year’s 23-man All-Australian team. But it was Dawson’s message about the importance of mental health after he tragically lost his older brother Jaryd Dawson during the year that was the most telling.

Jordan Dawson and Max Gawn. AFL Photos

“I think we saw leadership tonight,” Gawn said.

“I think for Jordan to get up and do what he did, to speak about mental health, to lead his side through the tragedy that happened to his family. And then to show vulnerability in front of a group of strangers that he hasn’t got it right, he hasn’t got it perfect with his battle right now, and asking for help – like that’s a captain that I want to be behind.”

The veteran Melbourne captain even half-joked that he was thankful for the “gesture” of being named captain of the AFL’s best team.

“So I appreciate the gesture, but I want to get behind Jordan Dawson, and I want to allow him to do the speech, because his speech was perfect tonight,” Gawn said.
